definition_zh: 偿还；还款；报答；回报
definition_en: to pay back money owed; to give something in return for kindness or injury
core_image: 一只张开的手掌接到钱，另一张手掌上的欠款数字随之变小
scene: 小方大学时向亲戚借了一笔钱，毕业工作的第一个月就想把它还掉。 He plans to repay the entire debt within two years.
sceneCN: 这里 repay 指「偿还借款」（第 1 个义项：归还所欠的钱）；句意为他计划在两年内还清全部债务。图中可辨识物件：借条、转账记录、日历。

pos.zh: 偿还；报答（及物/不及物均可）

senses.title: to pay back money
senses.definition: to give back money that was borrowed or owed
senses.definitionCN: 把借来的或欠下的钱还给对方
senses.example: She repaid the loan three months early.
senses.exampleCN: 她提前三个月还清了贷款。
senses.why: This is the basic re- + pay sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是 re- + pay 的基本义。

senses.title: to settle a debt
senses.definition: to discharge or settle an amount owed, whether money or another obligation
senses.definitionCN: 结清所欠金额，无论金钱或其他义务
senses.example: He repaid his debt to society by serving three years in prison.
senses.exampleCN: 他通过服刑三年来偿还对社会的债务。
senses.why: The monetary sense extends to any obligation one owes.
senses.whyCN: 金钱义延伸到任何亏欠的义务。

senses.title: to give back for kindness
senses.definition: to do or give something nice in return for a favour or kindness
senses.definitionCN: 为答谢恩惠或善意而做或给予美好的事物
senses.example: She repaid his kindness with a gift.
senses.exampleCN: 她用一份礼物来报答他的善意。
senses.why: 'Pay back' moves from money to gratitude.
senses.whyCN: pay back 从金钱走到了感激。

senses.title: to return with interest
senses.definition: to return more than was borrowed or received
senses.definitionCN: 返还的比借入或收到的多
senses.example: I'll repay your generosity with interest.
senses.exampleCN: 我会加倍报答你的慷慨。
senses.why: The idea of repaying interest extends to any generous return.
senses.whyCN: 偿还利息的想法延伸到任何慷慨的回报。

senses.title: to compensate for injury
senses.definition: to make up for a harm or injury done to someone
senses.definitionCN: 弥补对某人造成的伤害
senses.example: The family repaid the stranger's carelessness with anger.
senses.exampleCN: 那家人对陌生人的粗心给予了愤怒的「回报」。
senses.why: Paying back an injury is the dark side of the repay idea.
senses.whyCN: 偿还伤害是 repay 想法的阴暗面。

senses.title: to equal a benefit
senses.definition: to be worth enough to make up for a cost or sacrifice
senses.definitionCN: 价值足以弥补代价或牺牲
senses.example: The joys of teaching repay the long hours.
senses.exampleCN: 教书的乐趣足以回报那些漫长的工作时间。
senses.why: Abstract value makes up for cost, like a repayment.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的价值弥补代价，就像 repayment 一样。

senses.title: to refund
senses.definition: to give money back because of a return or cancellation
senses.definitionCN: 因退货或取消而把钱还给对方
senses.example: The shop repaid the full amount when the product broke.
senses.exampleCN: 产品损坏后商店全额退款。
senses.why: A refund is a kind of repayment for money received.
senses.whyCN: 退款是偿还已收金额的一种形式。

senses.title: to respond in kind
senses.definition: to respond to an action with a similar action
senses.definitionCN: 以类似的行动回应某个行动
senses.example: If he insults you, don't repay him in the same coin.
senses.exampleCN: 如果他骂你，不要以牙还牙。
senses.why: Paying back an action mirrors the structure of repaying money.
senses.whyCN: 偿还一个行为在结构上跟还钱一样。

intro.en: Repay is a transparent compound: re- 'back' + pay. Pay itself comes from Old French payer 'to appease', which comes from Latin pacare.
intro.cn: repay 是清晰的复合：re-「回」+ pay。pay 来自古法语 payer「安抚」，后者来自拉丁语 pacare。

items.en: Latin re- 'back, again' formed many Middle English compound verbs.
items.cn: 拉丁语 re-「回、再」在中古英语构成很多复合动词。

items.en: Old French payer came from Latin pacare 'to appease, make peace', built on pax 'peace'.
items.cn: 古法语 payer 来自拉丁语 pacare「使和平、安抚」，由 pax「和平」构成。

items.en: English pay entered around 1300 from Old French.
items.cn: 英语 pay 约 1300 年从古法语进入。

items.en: repay was formed by early Middle English (around 1300) as a transparent compound of re- + pay.
items.cn: repay 在早期中古英语（约 1300）由 re- + pay 构成，是清晰的复合。

items.en: The past tense and past participle repaid follows an irregular pattern: repay → repaid by analogy with pay → paid.
items.cn: 过去式和过去分词 repaid 按不规则形式：repay → repaid，类比 pay → paid。

items.en: All etymology solid; the 'appease' origin of pay is well established in historical lexicography.
items.cn: 全部词源可靠；pay「安抚」的起源在历史词典学中已充分确立。

note.en: Look-alikes share the pay root; near meanings are ways of giving something back.
note.cn: 形近共享 pay 词根；近义是把某物还给对方的各种方式。

entries.definition: To give money; repay adds 'back'.
entries.definitionCN: 付钱；repay 加了「回」。

entries.definition: To play again; same re- prefix, different second element.
entries.definitionCN: 再玩一次；同 re- 前缀，不同第二成分。

entries.definition: To show; no re- prefix, different compound.
entries.definitionCN: 展示；没有 re- 前缀，另一个复合。

entries.definition: The past tense of repay, irregular like paid.
entries.definitionCN: repay 的过去式，不规则，跟 paid 一样。

entries.definition: To give something back in general; repay is mostly money or kindness.
entries.definitionCN: 把东西还给对方，泛指；repay 多指钱或善意。

entries.definition: To give money back because of a return; repay covers any debt or kindness.
entries.definitionCN: 因退货而退钱；repay 覆盖任何债务或善意。

entries.definition: To compensate for harm or effort, not just money.
entries.definitionCN: 补偿伤害或努力，不限于金钱。

entries.definition: To respond to a favour with a favour; repay extends to money and harm too.
entries.definitionCN: 以恩惠回报恩惠；repay 也延伸到金钱和伤害。

normalIntro.en: Real roots and real compounds.
normalIntro.cn: 真实词根与真实复合。

normal.en: re- 'back' + pay 'to pay' = pay back.
normal.cn: re-「回」+ pay「付」= 付回去。

normal.en: pay ← French payer ← Latin pacare ← pax 'peace'; paying appeases a debt.
normal.cn: pay ← 法语 payer ← 拉丁语 pacare ← pax「和平」；付钱就是安抚债务。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: repay a loan, repay a favour, repay in full.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：repay a loan 还债、repay a favour 报恩、repay in full 全还。

normal.en: Irregular past: repay → repaid (like pay → paid).
normal.cn: 不规则过去式：repay → repaid（跟 pay → paid 一样）。

normal.en: repayment is the noun of this verb.
normal.cn: repayment 是这个动词的名词。

abstract.en: Picture a hand giving back coins while another hand's debt shrinks.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手还回硬币，另一只手上的欠款就变小。

abstract.en: Picture a Latin creditor saying 'pax!' after being paid.
abstract.cn: 想象一个罗马债主收到钱后喊一声「和平了！」。

abstract.en: Picture an X on the debt note that fades as repayments come in.
abstract.cn: 想象借条上的欠款随着每一次还款在变淡。

examples.en: He will repay the loan with monthly instalments over three years.
examples.cn: 他将在三年内按月分期偿还这笔贷款。

examples.en: She repaid her old teacher's encouragement by becoming an educator herself.
examples.cn: 她成为一名教育工作者，以此回报老恩师的鼓励。

examples.en: Will the joy of living abroad repay the disruption to her career?
examples.cn: 在国外生活的快乐能弥补事业上的中断吗？

dict_mnemonic.text: re-（回）+ pay（付）= 付回去 → 偿还

root: 拉丁语 re-「回」+ 古法语 payer「支付、安抚」（← 拉丁语 pacare ← pax「和平」）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses unfold: pay back money → settle any obligation → repay kindness → generous return → repay harm → abstract cost-benefit → refund → respond in kind.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项展开：还钱 → 结清任何义务 → 报答善意 → 慷慨回报 → 偿还伤害 → 抽象上的成本收益 → 退款 → 以同样方式回应。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one hand pushes coins into another, a debt note behind them loses value.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把硬币推给另一只手，身后的借条在贬值。

branches.en: THE MONETARY CORE: returning borrowed money.
branches.cn: 金钱核心：归还借来的钱。

branches.en: ANY OBLIGATION: debts to society, not only banks.
branches.cn: 任何义务：对社会的债，不只是银行。

branches.en: POSITIVE RETURNS: kindness rewarded, generosity returned with interest.
branches.cn: 正面回报：善意得到报答，慷慨得到加倍回报。

branches.en: NEGATIVE RETURNS: harm repaid, eye for an eye.
branches.cn: 负面回报：伤害被偿还，以牙还牙。

branches.en: ABSTRACT AND COMMERCIAL: abstract value repays a cost, refunds are a commercial repay.
branches.cn: 抽象与商业：抽象价值回报代价，退款是商业中的 repay。

intro.en: Repay is re- + pay. Pay comes from Latin pacare 'to appease' from pax 'peace'.
intro.cn: repay 是 re- + pay。pay 来自拉丁语 pacare「安抚」，后者来自 pax「和平」。

latinIntro.en: re- (Latin) + pay (← French payer ← Latin pacare ← pax).
latinIntro.cn: re-（拉丁）+ pay（← 法 payer ← 拉丁 pacare ← pax）。

items.example: re- is the direction component.
items.exampleCN: re- 是方向成分。

items.example: The ancient sense was appeasement.
items.exampleCN: 古代的意思是安抚。

items.example: Pacare was built on pax.
items.exampleCN: Pacare 由 pax 构成。

items.example: Paying was originally making peace with a creditor.
items.exampleCN: 付钱原本就是跟债主讲和。

items.example: The verb repays money, kindness or harm.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词可以偿还钱、善意或伤害。

items.example: Repayment is the noun of repay.
items.exampleCN: Repayment 是 repay 的名词。

items.example: Repayable means 'able to be repaid'.
items.exampleCN: repayable 意为「可被偿还的」。

items.example: Repaid follows the same irregular pattern.
items.exampleCN: Repaid 遵循同样的不规则形式。

items.example: Payee receives the repayment.
items.exampleCN: Payee 是收到 repayment 的人。

items.example: The payer of a repayment is the borrower.
items.exampleCN: repayment 的 payer 是借款人。

definition_zh: 战场；两军交战的地面；引申为任何斗争发生的领域
definition_en: the ground on which a battle is fought, and by extension any area or sphere where a struggle takes place
core_image: 被车辙压出深沟的田野，断栅与散落的盔甲之间，远处两面破旗还立着
scene: 清晨的田野上留着深深的车辙与断栅，散落的盔甲被露水打湿，远处两面破旗仍插在土里。 The battlefield lay silent after the last regiment withdrew.
sceneCN: 这里 battlefield 指「两军实际交战的那片地面」（第 1 个义项：战斗发生的地点本身）；句意为最后一支团撤退之后，战场一片寂静。图中可辨识物件：车辙、断栅、散落盔甲、远处两面破旗。

pos.zh: 战场；交战地带；斗争领域（可数；复数 battlefields）

derivatives.zh: 战斗；搏斗（古法语 bataille < 拉丁 battualia「士兵的击打练习」< battuere「击打」，battuere 更深来源不确定）
战场；争夺之地（battle 加 ground，由「战斗」转为「战斗发生的地面」）
营；作战单位（法语 bataillon < 意大利 battaglione，与 battaglia「战斗」同族，由「战斗」转为「战斗编制」）
田野；领域；实地（古英语 feld「开阔地」，由「开阔地」转为「活动领域」）
守场员（field 加 -er，指在场上负责某一区域的人）
守备；实地操作（field 加 -ing，指在场上或实地进行的过程）

senses.title: The ground of a battle
senses.definition: the actual piece of ground on which opposing forces meet and fight
senses.definitionCN: 敌对双方相遇并交战的真实地面
senses.example: The battlefield lay silent after the last regiment withdrew.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一支团撤退之后，战场一片寂静。
senses.why: Battle names the fighting and field names the open ground, so the compound is simply the ground where the fighting happens.
senses.whyCN: battle 指战斗，field 指开阔地面，因此这个复合词就是战斗发生的那片地面。

senses.title: The wider zone of combat
senses.definition: the larger area around the fighting, including approaches, reserves and rear positions
senses.definitionCN: 战斗周边更大的区域，包括接近路线、预备队与后方阵地
senses.example: The whole valley became a battlefield once the artillery found the range.
senses.exampleCN: 炮兵测准距离之后，整条山谷都成了战场。
senses.why: A battle spreads outward through artillery and movement, so the word expands from the meeting point to the whole contested zone.
senses.whyCN: 战斗会通过炮火与机动向外扩散，因此这个词从相遇点扩展到整片争夺地带。

senses.title: The scene after the fighting
senses.definition: the field as it is found afterwards, marked by wreckage, graves and abandoned equipment
senses.definitionCN: 战后被人看到的场地，遍布残骸、坟墓与丢弃的装备
senses.example: Photographers walked the battlefield at dawn, counting the wrecked guns.
senses.exampleCN: 摄影师在黎明时走过战场，清点被毁的火炮。
senses.why: Once the noise stops, the ground becomes a scene to be inspected, and the same word names that aftermath.
senses.whyCN: 枪炮声停止之后，这片地面变成可供查看的现场，同一个词就指这种战后景象。

senses.title: A figurative arena of struggle
senses.definition: any sphere in which rivals contend, such as politics, science or the market
senses.definitionCN: 竞争对手相争的任何领域，如政治、科学或市场
senses.example: The courtroom became the battlefield for two rival laboratories.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭成了两家竞争实验室的战场。
senses.why: The metaphor keeps the essentials of the literal scene: two sides, a contested space and a result that is won or lost.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留了字面场景的核心：两方、一片争夺的空间，以及一个分出胜负的结果。

senses.title: The electronic or cyber battlefield
senses.definition: the digital domain in which networks, signals and data are attacked and defended
senses.definitionCN: 对网络、信号与数据进行攻防的数字领域
senses.example: Engineers now map the cyber battlefield as carefully as any hill.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师如今像测绘任何一座山丘那样仔细地测绘网络战场。
senses.why: New domains inherit old words because the shape of attack, defence and terrain remains the same without soil.
senses.whyCN: 新领域会继承旧词，因为攻防与地形的结构在没有土壤时仍然相同。

senses.title: The negotiating table as a battlefield
senses.definition: a rhetorical use for a negotiation in which each concession is treated as ground gained or lost
senses.definitionCN: 修辞用法，指把每一次让步都视为得失地盘的谈判
senses.example: Both delegations treated the treaty talks as a battlefield of paragraphs.
senses.exampleCN: 两个代表团把条约谈判当成逐段争夺的战场。
senses.why: Negotiation has fronts, trenches and withdrawals in miniature, so speakers borrow the field to describe them.
senses.whyCN: 谈判以缩小的规模拥有前线、战壕与撤退，因此说话者借这片场地来描写它。

senses.title: A historic site and memorial
senses.titleCN: 作为历史遗址与纪念地
senses.definition: a preserved field visited for its monuments, graves and guided tours rather than for fighting
senses.definitionCN: 因纪念碑、墓地与导览而被参观的保存场地，而非用于作战
senses.example: The old battlefield is now a park with a visitors' centre.
senses.exampleCN: 这片旧战场如今是一座设有游客中心的公园。
senses.why: When the fighting is long past, the ground survives as a place of memory, and the word follows it into heritage.
senses.whyCN: 战斗久远之后，这片地面作为记忆之地留存下来，词义也随之进入遗产领域。

senses.title: The front line of hospitals or disasters
senses.titleCN: 医院或灾难中的前线比喻
senses.definition: a journalistic use for the place where medical staff or rescue workers face the heaviest pressure
senses.definitionCN: 新闻用法，指医护人员或救援人员承受最大压力的地方
senses.example: The emergency ward was the battlefield of the night shift.
senses.exampleCN: 急诊病房是夜班的前线战场。
senses.why: The word transfers wherever people hold a line under pressure, and a ward or a flood zone has exactly that line.
senses.whyCN: 只要人们顶着压力守住一条线，这个词就能迁移过去，而病房或洪区正有这样一条线。

intro.en: The compound joins a Latin-derived word for fighting to an Old English word for open land; the two halves are unrelated. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个复合词把一个源自拉丁语的「打斗」词与一个古英语的「开阔地」词连在一起，两半互不同源。年代均为约数。

items.en: Battuere meant 'to beat, strike'; its deeper origin is source uncertain, and no earlier root is reliably attested.
items.cn: battuere 意为「击打、敲打」；其更深来源属来源不确定，没有可靠书证的更早词根。

items.en: Battualia named the striking exercises of soldiers, and from that practice the word came to mean a fight.
items.cn: battualia 指士兵的击打演练，由这种练习引申为一场打斗。

items.en: Old French bataille carried the sense of a battle into English, where it named the engagement itself.
items.cn: 古法语 bataille 把「战斗」的含义带入英语，指交战本身。

items.en: Feld meant open land, a wide flat stretch, and it is the source of the field half of the compound.
items.cn: feld 指开阔地、大片平地，是这个复合词中 field 一半的来源。

items.en: English joined battle and field into one noun for the ground of an engagement, and the compound has kept that literal core.
items.cn: 英语把 battle 与 field 合成一个指交战地面的名词，这个复合词一直保留这一字面核心。

items.en: Source uncertain: the exact first written use of the compound is not recorded, and the deeper origin of battuere is a matter of reconstruction rather than attested fact.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这个复合词确切的最早书证没有记载，battuere 的更深来源属于重构而非有书证的事实。

note.en: Group one separates the two halves and the near-doublet from the compound; group two holds terms for the spaces where fighting is organized.
note.cn: 第一组把这个复合词的两半及近义双式词分开；第二组是用于组织作战的空间名称。

entries.definition: A single engagement between armed forces; the field is only the place where it happens.
entries.definitionCN: 指武装力量之间的一次交战；field 只是它发生的地点。

entries.definition: Open land or a sphere of activity; it need not be contested at all.
entries.definitionCN: 指开阔地或活动领域；它完全不必是被争夺的。

entries.definition: Essentially the same ground as battlefield, but it is the more common choice in political and commercial metaphors.
entries.definitionCN: 本质上与 battlefield 指同一片地面，但在政治与商业比喻中更常用。

entries.definition: A military unit, from the same Italian battle family; it is an organization of soldiers, not a place.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个军事单位，同出意大利语「战斗」词族；它是士兵的编制，不是地点。

entries.definition: The whole geographic area in which a war is conducted; a battlefield is one small part of it.
entries.definitionCN: 指进行一场战争的整个地理区域；battlefield 只是其中很小的一部分。

entries.definition: The moving line where opposing forces meet; it is a boundary, while a battlefield is an area.
entries.definitionCN: 指敌对力量相遇的移动界线；它是一条线，而 battlefield 是一片区域。

entries.definition: An area officially designated as dangerous because of fighting; the term is administrative as much as military.
entries.definitionCN: 指因交战而被正式划为危险的区域；这个词既是军事用语，也是行政用语。

entries.definition: A place or sphere of contest, from Latin arena 'sand'; it matches the figurative battlefield, not the literal one.
entries.definitionCN: 指较量之处或领域，出自拉丁 arena「沙」；它对应比喻性的 battlefield，而非字面战场。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Battle plus field is transparent: the fighting plus the open ground it happens on.
normal.cn: battle 加 field 结构透明：战斗加上它发生的开阔地面。

normal.en: The battle family runs battuere, battualia, bataille, battle, battalion, battleground.
normal.cn: 同族词依次是 battuere、battualia、bataille、battle、battalion、battleground。

normal.en: The field half is Old English feld 'open land', the same word that survives in field and fielder.
normal.cn: field 一半是古英语 feld「开阔地」，同一词还留在 field 与 fielder 中。

normal.en: Collocations mark the literal and the figurative: on the battlefield, battlefield medicine, the battlefield of ideas.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出字面与比喻：在战场上、战地医疗、思想战场。

normal.cn: 两半两个来源：battle 经法语来自拉丁语，field 是古英语，二者只在英语中相遇。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses spread from one field: the ground of the fight widens into a zone, becomes an aftermath, then serves as a metaphor for any contest, a cyber domain, a negotiating table, a heritage site and finally a hospital front line.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从同一片地面铺开：交战的地面扩成地带，变成战后现场，再被借作任何较量的比喻、网络领域、谈判桌、历史遗址，最后是医院前线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rutted field where two sides met, still carrying the marks of the encounter.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片布满车辙的田野，两方曾在此相遇，地上仍留着交手的痕迹。

branches.en: POINT AND ZONE: the meeting ground and the wider contested area are the same field at two scales.
branches.cn: 交点与地带：相遇的地面与更广的争夺区域，是同一片场地在两种尺度上的样子。

branches.en: AFTERMATH AND METAPHOR: what is found afterwards becomes the image for any struggle elsewhere.
branches.cn: 现场与比喻：战后所见的景象，变成别处任何斗争的形象。

branches.en: NEW DOMAINS: networks and negotiating tables inherit the field because attack and defence keep their shape.
branches.cn: 新领域：网络与谈判桌继承了这片场地，因为攻与守的结构不变。

branches.en: HERITAGE: the fighting ends, and the ground survives as a place to visit and remember.
branches.cn: 遗产：战斗结束，这片地面作为可参观、可记忆之处留存下来。

branches.en: FRONT LINE: wards and flood zones repeat the literal line under pressure.
branches.cn: 前线：病房与洪区在压力下重演了那条字面意义的线。

intro.en: The compound is made of two unrelated pieces: a Latin-derived battle word and an Old English field word.

definition_zh: （使）相关；使相互关联；对应；并置比对
definition_en: to have a mutual relation, or to place two sets of things so that they match
core_image: 两条曲线画在同一张方格纸上，一条升高时另一条也跟着升高，起落彼此对齐
scene: 研究者把十年的降雨记录与河流流量并排画在同一张图上，两条线几乎同步起落。 Researchers correlate rainfall records with river flow over ten years.
sceneCN: 这里指把两组记录并排摆放，使对应项彼此对齐（第 5 个义项：把两组数据或记录对齐比对）；句意：研究者把十年的降雨记录与河流流量对应起来看。

pos.zh: 相关；相互关联
使关联；把……对应起来

senses.title: Of two things varying together
senses.definition: of two quantities or facts, to change together in a way that can be observed
senses.definitionCN: 指两个数量或事实以可观察的方式一同变化
senses.example: Height and weight correlate across the whole population.
senses.exampleCN: 在整个人群中，身高与体重是相关的。
senses.why: The prefix means together and the root means carried back, so two things are carried back to each other.
senses.whyCN: 前缀表示一起，词根表示带回，因此两样东西彼此被带回对照。

senses.title: To show a statistical correlation
senses.definition: to establish by measurement that two variables move together more than chance would explain
senses.definitionCN: 通过测量确定两个变量的同向变化超出偶然所能解释的范围
senses.example: The survey correlates income with years of schooling.
senses.exampleCN: 这项调查把收入与受教育年限联系起来。
senses.why: Statistics turned the mutual relation into a coefficient, and the verb took on the measuring sense.
senses.whyCN: 统计学把相互关联变成一个系数，这个动词也就有了测量的含义。

senses.title: To connect things in the mind
senses.titleCN: 在心里把事物联系起来
senses.definition: to bring two ideas into a mental link so that one calls up the other
senses.definitionCN: 把两个观念在心里连起来，使一个能唤起另一个
senses.example: Children correlate the sound of the bell with the end of class.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们把铃声与下课联系起来。
senses.why: The mind carries one idea back to another, which is the same movement the Latin root names.
senses.whyCN: 心智把一个观念带回另一个，这正是那个拉丁词根所命名的动作。

senses.title: To correspond to each other
senses.definition: of two series or accounts, to match item by item so that each has a partner
senses.definitionCN: 指两个序列或两份陈述逐项吻合，各自都有对应项
senses.example: The numbered seals correlate with the entries in the catalogue.
senses.exampleCN: 带编号的印章与目录中的条目一一对应。
senses.why: The preposition with marks the second term of the pair, and the verb simply reports that the pair fits.
senses.whyCN: 介词标明这一对中的第二项，动词只报告这一对彼此吻合。

senses.title: To line up two sets of records
senses.definition: to arrange two sets of data or documents so that matching items stand side by side
senses.definitionCN: 把两组数据或文件排列好，使相配的项目彼此并排
senses.example: Researchers correlate rainfall records with river flow over ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 研究者把十年的降雨记录与河流流量对应起来看。
senses.why: Records are correlated when one column is laid against another, which is the manual act behind the statistics.
senses.whyCN: 当一列数据对着另一列摆好，记录就被对齐了，这是统计背后的手工动作。

senses.title: To match rock layers across regions
senses.titleCN: 把不同地区的岩层对应起来
senses.definition: in geology, to identify layers in separate places as the same age or origin
senses.definitionCN: 在地质学中，判定不同地点的地层属于同一时代或同一来源
senses.example: Geologists correlate the sandstone beds on both sides of the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 地质学家把河谷两侧的砂岩层对应起来。
senses.why: Strata are matched by their fossils and grain, the same lining-up act carried out on a landscape.
senses.whyCN: 地层靠化石与颗粒特征配对，就是把对齐动作放到整片地貌上。

senses.title: Of traits that vary together in species
senses.definition: in biology, of two traits or structures, to occur together across related organisms
senses.definitionCN: 在生物学中，指两种性状或结构在亲缘生物中相伴出现
senses.example: Wing length and body size correlate in these birds.
senses.exampleCN: 在这些鸟身上，翅长与体型大小是相关的。
senses.why: Living things supply paired measurements too, so the statistical sense extends to natural variation.
senses.whyCN: 生物同样提供成对的测量值，统计义便延伸到自然变异。

senses.title: To compare findings across studies
senses.titleCN: 在多项研究之间做对应比较
senses.definition: to bring results from separate studies into one comparison so that agreement or conflict shows
senses.definitionCN: 把不同研究的结果放进同一次比较，使一致或冲突之处显现
senses.example: The review correlates the findings of twelve field studies.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇综述把十二项实地研究的发现对应比较。
senses.why: Research synthesis is a large-scale version of laying two records side by side.
senses.whyCN: 研究综合就是把两份记录并排摆放这一动作的放大版。

intro.en: Correlate joins a prefix meaning together to the Latin participle of the verb for carrying back. Medieval Latin used the pair for things that answer to each other, and statistics gave the word its modern measuring sense.
intro.cn: 本词把表示一起的前缀接在拉丁语中表示带回的动词分词上。中世纪拉丁语用这一对词指彼此呼应之物，统计学又给了它现代的测量含义。

items.en: Referre meant to carry back or to bring into relation, and its participle is the second half of this word.
items.cn: 这个拉丁动词意为带回或使发生关联，它的分词就是本词的后半截。

items.en: The prefix com- meant together, so the compound said carried back together, that is, set in a mutual relation.
items.cn: 前缀表示一起，因此复合词意为被一起带回，也就是被摆进相互关系。

items.en: Medieval Latin used the form for things that correspond, especially in grammar and theology.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语用这个形式指彼此对应之物，尤其见于语法与神学。

items.en: Nineteenth-century statistics made correlation a measured relation between two variables.
items.cn: 十九世纪的统计学把相关变成两个变量之间可测量的关系。

items.en: English took the verb in the nineteenth century, chiefly in scientific and academic writing.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪借入这个动词，主要用于科学与学术写作。

items.en: Geology, biology and research synthesis later applied the same alignment to strata, traits and whole studies.
items.cn: 地质学、生物学与研究综合后来把同一种对齐动作用于地层、性状与整项研究。

note.en: The first group shares the carrying-back root or its family forms; the second group names nearby kinds of matching. Correlate reports that two things vary or line up together, while corroborate reports that evidence makes a claim stronger, so relation and proof must not be confused.
note.cn: 第一组共享带回词根或其词族形式；第二组是相邻的配对类型。本词说的是两件事一同变化或彼此对齐，佐证类词说的是证据把某个说法坐实，关系与证明不能混为一谈。

entries.definition: The measured relation between two things, or the act of aligning them.
entries.definitionCN: 两事物之间被测量的关系，或把它们对齐的动作。

entries.definition: Mutually related, and in grammar a paired word such as either and or.
entries.definitionCN: 相互关联的；语法上指成对出现的词。

entries.definition: Considered in relation to something else; it stops short of measuring a pair.
entries.definitionCN: 相对于某物而言的；并未达到测量一对关系的程度。

entries.definition: To connect or to tell; it is the plainer verb behind the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 连接或讲述；是名词背后更平实的动词。

entries.definition: To match or to exchange letters; matching is by form or position, not by measured variation.
entries.definitionCN: 相配或通信；匹配依据形式或位置，而非测量出的共同变化。

entries.definition: To link in thought or in company; no measurement is implied.
entries.definitionCN: 在思想上或交往中联系；不牵涉测量。

entries.definition: To join or to show a link; it is the general word for any linkage.
entries.definitionCN: 连接或显示联系；是任何联系的泛称。

entries.definition: To put two things together because they are alike; the judgement is identity, not variation.
entries.definitionCN: 因相似而把两物配在一起；判断的是相同，而非共变。

entries.definition: To fall on the same point or time; coincidence is exact, correlation is statistical.
entries.definitionCN: 落在同一点或同一时刻；重合是精确的，相关是统计的。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the carrying-back root, the real family and the preposition that marks the second term.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用带回词根、真实同族词，以及标记第二项的介词。

normal.en: The root means carried back, so two things are carried back to each other for comparison.
normal.cn: 词根意为带回，两样东西被带回到彼此面前作比较。

normal.en: The family runs correlation, correlative, correlated and correlational.
normal.cn: 同族词有相关、对应的、相关的与相关性研究的。

normal.en: The preposition is with: one thing correlates with another.
normal.cn: 介词用与：一事物与另一事物相关。

normal.en: Statistics supplies the number, but the everyday sense needs no number at all.
normal.cn: 统计学提供数值，但日常义完全不需要数值。

normal.en: The geological sense is a large-scale version: whole layers matched across a valley.
normal.cn: 地质义是放大版：整层岩层跨越河谷彼此对应。

abstract.cn: 想象两名舞者从不接触，却总在同一瞬间转身。

examples.en: The two lists correlate neatly once the dates are aligned.

examples.cn: 研究者把土壤酸度与作物产量对应起来分析。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「可」加「瑞」加「累特」——两条线一起起落，像被同一根绳拉着：相关

root: 拉丁语「带回」动词的分词加「一起」前缀，中世纪拉丁语指彼此对应之物，十九世纪经统计学获得「相关」的测量含义。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one alignment: variables varying together, a measured coefficient, mental association, item-by-item matching, records laid side by side, rock layers, paired traits and pooled studies.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一种对齐：变量共同变化、测出的系数、心里的联想、逐项对应、并排的记录、岩层、成对的性状，以及汇总的研究。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two curves drawn on one sheet of graph paper, rising and falling together.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条曲线画在同一张方格纸上，一条升高时另一条也跟着升高，起落彼此对齐。

branches.en: THE MEASURED RELATION: things varying together, and the coefficient that records it.
branches.cn: 被测量的关系：事物共同变化，以及记录它的系数。

branches.en: THE MIND: one idea calling up another without any number.
branches.cn: 心智：一个观念唤起另一个，不涉及数值。

branches.en: THE ALIGNMENT: series corresponding item by item, and records laid side by side.
branches.cn: 对齐：序列逐项对应，记录并排摆放。

branches.en: THE NATURAL WORLD: rock layers matched across a valley and traits paired across a species.
branches.cn: 自然世界：跨越河谷对应的岩层，以及物种中成对的性状。

branches.en: THE LITERATURE: separate studies brought into one comparison.
branches.cn: 文献：多项研究被放进同一次比较。

intro.en: Correlate is a Latin compound of togetherness and carrying back, and its family supplies the noun, the adjective and the plainer verb of relation.
intro.cn: 本词是表示「一起」与「带回」的拉丁复合词，其词族提供名词、形容词，以及更平实的关联动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin referre and its participle relatus supply the second half; com- supplies the first.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中表示带回的动词及其分词提供后半截，前缀提供前半截。

items.example: It makes the carrying mutual.
items.exampleCN: 它使「带回」成为相互的。

items.example: The verb supplies the second half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供复合词的后半截。

items.example: The participle is the shape English actually took over.
items.exampleCN: 英语实际接收的是这个分词形式。

items.example: Medieval writers added the prefix to the participle.
items.exampleCN: 中世纪作者在这个分词前加了前缀。

items.example: It turns the Latin stem into the English verb.
items.exampleCN: 它把拉丁词干变成英语动词。

items.example: It builds the name of the measured relation.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示被测量关系的名词。

items.example: It builds the adjective for paired items.
items.exampleCN: 它构成描述成对项目的形容词。

items.example: It builds the adjective for studies of correlation.
items.exampleCN: 它构成描述相关性研究的形容词。

latinEntries.meaning: to carry back, to bring into relation

definition_zh: 远缘繁殖；远交；与亲缘较远的个体交配繁殖
definition_en: breeding between individuals that are not closely related, especially in order to increase genetic variation in the offspring
core_image: 两片相距很远的林地里的个体被牵到一起，把各自的血统带进同一个后代
scene: 育种站把来自两片相距很远的林地的个体配到一起，用远缘繁殖提高后代的遗传多样性。 At the breeding station, individuals from two woodlands far apart are paired in outbreeding to raise the genetic diversity of their offspring.
sceneCN: 这里 outbreeding 是「与亲缘关系较远的个体交配繁殖」（第 1 个义项：远缘个体之间的配对繁殖）；句意：育种站把来自两片相距很远林地的个体配到一起，用远缘繁殖提高后代的遗传多样性。

pos.zh: 远缘繁殖；远交（与近亲繁殖相对，多作不可数）

senses.title: Mate with a distantly related partner
senses.titleCN: 与亲缘较远的个体交配
senses.definition: to breed with an individual that is not a close relative, so that the young receive genes from two separate lines
senses.definitionCN: 与并非近亲的个体繁殖，使后代获得来自两条独立血统的基因
senses.example: Zoos plan outbreeding to keep captive herds healthy.
senses.exampleCN: 动物园规划远缘交配，以保持圈养群体的健康。
senses.why: Out- is the native English prefix for 'outside, beyond', so outbreeding names mating that reaches outside the circle of close kin; the compound is English, not Latin.
senses.whyCN: out- 是英语本族前缀，意为「在外、超出」，因此 outbreeding 指把配对对象选到近亲圈之外；这个词是英语复合词，并非拉丁借词。

senses.title: Raise heterozygosity in genetics
senses.definition: in genetics, the mating of unrelated individuals so that many gene loci become heterozygous in the offspring
senses.definitionCN: 遗传学中让无亲缘个体交配，使后代许多基因座位呈杂合状态
senses.example: Outbreeding raised heterozygosity at loci that had been fixed in the isolated herd.
senses.exampleCN: 远缘交配使这个隔离群体中原本固定的基因座位变为杂合。
senses.why: Genetics borrowed the word and made it quantitative: the further apart the parents, the more loci arrive heterozygous, so the term now names a genetic effect rather than a pedigree.
senses.whyCN: 遗传学借用了这个词并使它可以量化：亲本相距越远，后代杂合的座位越多，因此这个词现在指一种遗传效应，而不只是谱系关系。

senses.title: A livestock breeding practice
senses.titleCN: 家畜育种中的一项做法
senses.definition: the practice of bringing an unrelated sire or dam into a herd to refresh its bloodlines
senses.definitionCN: 把无亲缘的公畜或母畜引入畜群、以更新其血统的做法
senses.example: Cattle breeders use outbreeding to bring new bloodlines into a closed herd.
senses.exampleCN: 养牛者用远缘交配把新的血统引入封闭的畜群。
senses.why: Herd books set inbreeding against outbreeding to describe breeding plans, and the word settled into the vocabulary of livestock improvement.
senses.whyCN: 畜群登记簿用近交与远交对举来描述繁殖计划，这个词于是进入了家畜改良的术语体系。

senses.title: Crossing inbred lines in plant breeding
senses.titleCN: 植物育种中杂交自交系
senses.definition: in plant breeding, the crossing of genetically distinct inbred lines to obtain vigorous hybrids
senses.definitionCN: 植物育种中把遗传上不同的自交系杂交，以获得长势旺盛的杂种
senses.example: Plant breeders rely on outbreeding when two inbred lines are crossed.
senses.exampleCN: 植物育种者把两个自交系杂交时，依靠的正是远缘繁殖。
senses.why: Plant breeders also say outcrossing for the same act; outbreeding is the general term, and the two are often used side by side in applied genetics.
senses.whyCN: 植物育种者也用 outcrossing 指同一做法；outbreeding 是总称，二者在应用遗传学文献里常并列使用。

senses.title: A remedy for inbreeding depression
senses.definition: the introduction of unrelated mates into a small isolated population whose fitness has fallen through inbreeding
senses.definitionCN: 向因近交而适合度下降的小型隔离群体引入无亲缘配偶
senses.example: Conservationists recommend outbreeding once the island population shows inbreeding depression.
senses.exampleCN: 一旦岛上群体出现近交衰退，保护工作者就建议采用远缘交配。
senses.why: Conservation biology reversed the old assumption that any crossing is good: outbreeding is prescribed when a small population shows inbreeding depression.
senses.whyCN: 保护生物学纠正了过去「任何杂交都好」的假设：只有当小群体出现近交衰退时，才指定采用远缘交配。

senses.title: The technical opposite of inbreeding
senses.titleCN: 与近亲繁殖构成的技术对立项
senses.definition: the mating pattern defined chiefly by contrast with inbreeding, namely pairing outside rather than inside the family line
senses.definitionCN: 主要指与近亲繁殖相对立的交配方式，即在家族线之外而非之内配对
senses.example: The pedigree records both inbreeding and outbreeding across five generations.
senses.exampleCN: 这份谱系记录跨越五代，把近交与远交都记了下来。
senses.why: The word exists mainly as the opposite of inbreeding, so its meaning is fixed by the contrast: mate outside the family line rather than inside it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词主要通过作为 inbreeding 的反义词而存在，其意义由对比确定：在家族线外交配，而不是在内。

senses.title: Outbreeding depression: too distant is harmful
senses.titleCN: 远交衰退：过远反而有害
senses.definition: a loss of fitness in hybrids whose parents came from populations carrying incompatible gene combinations
senses.definitionCN: 亲本来自携带不相容基因组合的群体时，杂种适合度下降的现象
senses.example: Outbreeding can lower fitness when distant populations carry incompatible gene complexes.
senses.exampleCN: 当相距很远的群体携带不相容的基因组合时，远缘交配可能降低适合度。
senses.why: Because distant populations may carry incompatible gene complexes, outbreeding has a negative branch, outbreeding depression, where hybrid fitness falls.
senses.whyCN: 由于相距很远的群体可能携带不相容的基因组合，远缘交配有一个负面分支，即远交衰退：杂种的适合度反而下降。

senses.title: A natural mating pattern in the wild
senses.definition: a mating pattern produced without a breeder, for example by dispersal or by mate choice that avoids relatives
senses.definitionCN: 无需育种者介入、由扩散或避开亲属的择偶行为形成的交配格局
senses.example: Dispersal serves as a natural outbreeding mechanism in many wind-pollinated plants.
senses.exampleCN: 对许多风媒植物来说，扩散就是天然的远缘繁殖机制。
senses.why: In wild plants and animals, dispersal and mate choice perform outbreeding without a breeder, so the term also names a natural mating pattern.
senses.whyCN: 在野生动植物中，扩散与择偶无需育种者即可完成远缘交配，因此这个词也指一种自然交配格局。

intro.en: Outbreeding is a native English compound, not a Latin borrowing: out- 'outside' plus breeding, from Old English brēdan 'to brood, hatch'. No Latin relative exists, so latinEntries is left empty. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: outbreeding 是英语本族复合词，并非拉丁借词：out-「在外」加 breeding，后者源自古英语 brēdan「孵、育」。本词没有拉丁同族，因此拉丁同族词条列表留空。年代均为约数。

items.en: The native verb brēdan meant 'to brood, to hatch, to warm', and its derivative brēding gave the noun breeding 'the act of producing young'.
items.cn: 本族动词 brēdan 意为「孵、抱窝、使暖」，其派生形式 brēding 给出名词 breeding「育幼的行为」。

items.en: By the Middle English period breeding covered the raising of animals and plants as well as hatching, and the sense 'reproduction controlled by humans' was in place.
items.cn: 到中古英语时期，breeding 已不仅指孵卵，还指饲养动植物，「由人控制繁殖」的意思也已经出现。

items.en: Out- is the native prefix meaning 'outside, beyond'; it marks the direction of the mating, away from the close family circle.
items.cn: out- 是英语本族前缀，意为「在外、超出」；它标出交配的方向，即离开近亲圈。

items.en: Nineteenth-century herd books set inbreeding against outbreeding, and the contrast fixed the word in livestock breeding.
items.cn: 19 世纪的畜群登记簿把近交与远交对举，这一对比使该词在家畜育种中固定下来。

items.en: Twentieth-century genetics made outbreeding a measurable event: the pairing of unrelated individuals to raise heterozygosity and mask recessive defects.
items.cn: 20 世纪遗传学使远缘繁殖成为可测量的事件：让无亲缘个体配对，以提高杂合度、掩盖隐性缺陷。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the exact year when the compound outbreeding first appeared in print is not established here, and no Latin source exists for the word.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：outbreeding 这一复合词最早见于印刷品的确切年份此处无法确定；该词也没有拉丁语来源。

note.en: Group one holds the breeding terms that are constantly confused; group two holds near neighbours that name a crossing or its result.
note.cn: 第一组是极易混淆的繁殖术语；第二组是表示杂交行为或其结果、语义相近的词。

entries.definition: Breeding between close relatives. In- 'inside' marks mating within the family line, exactly the direction outbreeding avoids.
entries.definitionCN: 近亲之间的繁殖。in-「在内」标出家族线之内的交配，正是 outbreeding 所要避开的方向。

entries.definition: The crossing of two unrelated lines, the usual term in plant and animal breeding for what outbreeding names in general.
entries.definitionCN: 两个无亲缘品系的杂交，是动植物育种中对应 outbreeding 总称的常用具体说法。

entries.definition: The verb behind the noun: to mate an individual with one outside its close kin. Outbreeding is simply the action noun.
entries.definitionCN: 名词背后的动词：使个体与近亲圈之外的个体交配。outbreeding 只是该动作的名词形式。

entries.definition: Crossing between different breeds or varieties, not necessarily distant relatives. It is broader in scope than outbreeding.
entries.definitionCN: 不同品种或变种之间的杂交，亲缘未必很远；范围比 outbreeding 更宽。

entries.definition: The production of hybrids, often between different species. Outbreeding normally stays within one species.
entries.definitionCN: 产生杂种的过程，常指不同物种之间；outbreeding 通常仍在同一物种内。

entries.definition: Deliberate mating to a particular ancestor's line, a controlled form of inbreeding rather than its opposite.
entries.definitionCN: 有意向某一祖先血统靠拢的配种，是受控的近交形式，而非其反面。

entries.definition: The movement of genes from one population or species into another through repeated crossing. It names the genetic result, not the breeding plan.
entries.definitionCN: 基因通过反复杂交从一个群体或物种流入另一个。它指遗传结果，而非配种方案。

entries.definition: The variety of alleles in a population, which outbreeding is used to raise; it is the aim, not the method.
entries.definitionCN: 群体中等位基因的多样性，正是远缘繁殖所要提高的对象；它是目的，不是方法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: out- 'outside' + breeding: mating that reaches outside the close family circle.
normal.cn: out-「在外」+ breeding：把配对对象选到近亲圈之外。

normal.en: The herd-book pair is inbreeding versus outbreeding, so the two words define each other.
normal.cn: 畜群登记簿里的对举是 inbreeding 与 outbreeding，两个词互相定义。

normal.en: Applied genetics also says outcrossing; the two terms often stand side by side in breeding manuals.
normal.cn: 应用遗传学也说 outcrossing；两个术语在育种手册里常并列出现。

normal.en: The negative branch has its own name: outbreeding depression, the mirror image of hybrid vigour.
normal.cn: 负面分支有自己的名称：outbreeding depression 远交衰退，正好与杂种优势相对。

normal.en: Outbreed, outbred and outbreeder are the verb, the participle and the person noun of the same family.
normal.cn: outbreed、outbred 与 outbreeder 是同一词族的动词、分词与施事名词。

abstract.en: Picture two orchards on opposite hills sending pollen to each other across the valley.
abstract.cn: 想象两座相对山坡上的果园隔着河谷互相送粉。

abstract.en: Picture a locked herd book with a new page ruled for a stranger's line.
abstract.cn: 想象一本锁着的畜群登记簿翻出新的一页，留给外来血统。

abstract.en: Picture a small island population that stops weakening once outsiders arrive.
abstract.cn: 想象一个海岛小群体，在外来个体到来后不再衰弱。

examples.en: The recovery plan set a minimum outbreeding distance between the two reserves.
examples.cn: 恢复计划为两个保护区之间规定了最小的远交距离。

examples.en: Too much outbreeding can break up gene combinations that local conditions had favoured.
examples.cn: 远缘交配过度会拆散本地环境原本偏爱的基因组合。

examples.en: Farmers describe outbreeding simply as bringing in a new bull from another district.
examples.cn: 农户把远缘繁殖简单说成从别的地区引进一头新公牛。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥特的育种」——把外头的血统引进来 → outbreeding 远缘繁殖

root: 英语本族复合词：out-（在外、向外）+ breeding（繁殖，源自古英语 brēdan「孵、育」）；无拉丁词根，拉丁同族词条列表留空。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of outbreeding all describe one move: a mate is brought in from outside the circle of close kin, and the effects of that move are then read in pedigrees, in heterozygosity, in hybrid vigour and finally in its failure.
sensesIntro.cn: outbreeding 的八个义项都描述同一个动作：从近亲圈之外引入配偶，随后这一动作的后果被分别读成谱系记录、杂合度、杂种优势，最后是它的失败。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two separate bloodlines meeting in one offspring, with the family circle left behind.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条彼此分离的血统在一个后代身上会合，近亲圈被留在身后。

branches.en: THE DEFINITION BY CONTRAST: outbreeding is what inbreeding is not, so the pair fixes the meaning.
branches.cn: 以对比定义：远缘繁殖就是近交的反面，两个词互为定义。

branches.en: MEASURABLE MIXING: genetics turns the pedigree move into a count of heterozygous loci.
branches.cn: 可测量的混合：遗传学把谱系上的动作变成杂合座位的计数。

branches.en: APPLIED CROSSING: plant breeders cross inbred lines and harvest the vigour.
branches.cn: 应用杂交：植物育种者杂交自交系，收获杂种优势。

branches.en: TWO OUTCOMES: bringing in outsiders can rescue a small population or break up co-adapted genes.
branches.cn: 两种结局：引入外来者既能挽救小群体，也可能拆散共适应的基因组合。

branches.en: WILD COUNTERPART: dispersal does the breeder's work without a breeder.
branches.cn: 野外的对应机制：扩散在没有育种者时完成了育种者的事。

intro.en: Outbreeding is a native compound whose two parts are both transparent English morphemes; the list shows how each part and each relative behaves.
intro.cn: outbreeding 是本族复合词，两个部分都是透明的英语语素；下表逐个说明各成分与同族词的作用。

latinIntro.en: This word has no Latin counterpart: it is formed from native English stock, so latinEntries is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: 本词没有拉丁语对应成分，由英语本族词素构成，因此拉丁同族词条列表留空。

items.example: Out- sends the mating outside the close family circle.
items.exampleCN: out- 把交配方向送到近亲圈之外。

items.example: Breeding is the general act that outbreeding qualifies.
items.exampleCN: breeding 是远缘繁殖所限定的那个总动作。

items.meaning: to mate outside the close kin
items.example: Keepers outbreed the captive group every third generation.
items.exampleCN: 饲养者每三代为圈养群体做一次远交。

items.example: The outbred pups were heavier at birth.
items.exampleCN: 远交产生的幼崽出生时更重。

items.meaning: a breeder or an individual that mates out
items.example: The outbreeder matched animals from different valleys.
items.exampleCN: 这位远交育种者把不同河谷的动物配对。

items.example: Inbreeding raised the frequency of a recessive defect.
items.exampleCN: 近交提高了隐性缺陷的出现频率。

items.example: Outcrossing restored yield in the depleted variety.
items.exampleCN: 异系交配恢复了衰退品种的产量。

items.example: Crossbreeding of two cattle breeds is common in the region.
items.exampleCN: 两个牛品种的杂交在该地区很常见。

definition_zh: 湿度；空气中水汽的含量；（常指）相对湿度
definition_en: the amount of water vapour in the air, usually reported as relative humidity
core_image: 一块湿布挂在封闭房间里，窗玻璃上凝着一层细小的水珠
scene: 梅雨季的午后，墙上挂着的毛巾一直不干，窗玻璃蒙着一层水汽。 Humidity in the valley stayed above ninety per cent for a week.
sceneCN: 这里 humidity 指「空气中水汽的含量」（第 1 个义项：湿度总称）；句意为这个山谷的湿度连续一周超过九成。图中可辨识物件：湿毛巾、蒙雾的窗玻璃、水珠、温度计。

pos.zh: 湿度；潮湿（不可数名词）
相对湿度（天气报告中常省略「相对」）

forms.label: 复数（不同环境的湿度值）

senses.title: Water vapour in the air
senses.definition: the amount of water vapour present in the air
senses.definitionCN: 空气中水汽的含量
senses.example: Humidity in the valley stayed above ninety per cent for a week.
senses.exampleCN: 这个山谷的湿度连续一周超过九成。
senses.why: Latin humiditas named moistness, and meteorology narrowed it to vapour in the air.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 humiditas 本指潮湿，气象学把它收窄为空气中的水汽。

senses.title: Relative humidity
senses.definition: the ratio of actual vapour to the maximum the air could hold at that temperature
senses.definitionCN: 实际水汽与该温度下空气所能容纳最大水汽的比值
senses.example: At thirty degrees, a relative humidity of eighty per cent feels far hotter.
senses.exampleCN: 在三十度时，八成相对湿度让人感觉热得多。
senses.why: weather reports need a ratio that people can feel, so the relative form became the default.
senses.whyCN: 天气报告需要一个能被人感受到的比值，相对湿度因此成了默认说法。

senses.title: Absolute humidity
senses.definition: the mass of water vapour in a given volume of air
senses.definitionCN: 一定体积空气中所含水汽的质量
senses.example: Absolute humidity is measured in grams per cubic metre.
senses.exampleCN: 绝对湿度以每立方米克数计量。
senses.why: engineering needs an amount rather than a ratio, so the absolute form is named separately.
senses.whyCN: 工程需要的是量而非比值，绝对湿度因此单独命名。

senses.title: Specific humidity
senses.definition: the mass of vapour per unit mass of moist air
senses.definitionCN: 每单位质量湿空气中所含水汽的质量
senses.example: Specific humidity changes little when air rises and cools.
senses.exampleCN: 空气上升冷却时，比湿变化很小。
senses.why: meteorology prefers a measure that survives compression and expansion, hence the per-mass form.
senses.whyCN: 气象学偏爱一种在压缩与膨胀中仍稳定的量，于是有了按质量计的形式。

senses.title: Humidity as a felt quality
senses.definition: the uncomfortable dampness felt when the air is warm and full of vapour
senses.definitionCN: 空气温暖且饱含水汽时令人不适的潮湿感
senses.example: The humidity made the whole afternoon feel sticky.
senses.exampleCN: 这种湿度让整个下午都黏糊糊的。
senses.why: the measured quantity also has a felt side, and everyday speech uses the word for that.
senses.whyCN: 这个可测的量也有体感的一面，日常语言就用这个词来指那种感觉。

senses.title: A figure in a weather report
senses.titleCN: 天气报告中的湿度指标
senses.definition: the percentage or value reported alongside temperature in a forecast
senses.definitionCN: 预报中与温度并列报告的那个百分数或数值
senses.example: The forecast gave thirty-two degrees and high humidity.
senses.exampleCN: 预报给出三十二度与高湿度。
senses.why: a forecast needs a compact number, and humidity became one of its standard figures.
senses.whyCN: 预报需要一个紧凑的数字，湿度成了它的标准数值之一。

senses.title: A controlled target indoors
senses.definition: the humidity level maintained in a greenhouse, museum, hospital or home
senses.definitionCN: 温室、博物馆、医院或住宅中维持的湿度水平
senses.example: The archive keeps humidity steady to protect the paper.
senses.exampleCN: 档案馆保持湿度稳定以保护纸张。
senses.why: materials need a narrow band of moisture, so buildings and museums control the value.
senses.whyCN: 材料需要一个很窄的水汽区间，建筑与博物馆因此控制这个数值。

senses.title: Effects on materials and health
senses.titleCN: 湿度对材料与健康的影响
senses.definition: the practical effects of moisture on wood, metal, lungs and skin
senses.definitionCN: 水汽对木材、金属、肺与皮肤的实际影响
senses.example: High humidity warped the floorboards within a season.
senses.exampleCN: 高湿度在一个季度内就让地板变形。
senses.why: the quantity has consequences, and the word extends to those consequences in building and health science.
senses.whyCN: 这个量有后果，这个词就延伸到建筑与健康科学中的这些后果。

intro.en: Humidity comes from Latin humiditas, a noun from humidus 'moist', itself from humere 'to be moist'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: humidity 来自拉丁 humiditas，它是 humidus「潮湿的」的名词形式，而 humidus 出自 humere「潮湿」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Humere meant 'to be moist'. Its deeper origin is not established, and the Indo-European root often cited for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: humere 意为「潮湿」。其更深来源未得到证明，常为它引用的印欧词根属于重构形式。

items.en: Humidus 'moist, wet' was the adjective from humere; it existed beside a variant umidus.
items.cn: humidus「潮湿的」是由 humere 构成的形容词，并与变体 umidus 并存。

items.en: Humiditas 'moistness' added the noun suffix to humidus and named the quality rather than a thing.
items.cn: humiditas「潮湿」在 humidus 上加名词后缀，指性质而非具体事物。

items.en: English humidity appears in the sixteenth century, borrowed through French from the Latin noun, and first meant dampness in general.
items.cn: 英语 humidity 在十六世纪出现，经法语从拉丁名词借入，最初泛指潮湿。

items.en: From the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries humidity became a measured quantity of vapour in the air, with relative and absolute forms.
items.cn: 从十八、十九世纪起，humidity 成为空气中水汽的可测数量，并有相对与绝对两种形式。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin and first date): the pre-Latin source of humere is not established, and the first English date is usually given as the 1530s but is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与首见年代）：humere 在拉丁语之前的来源未得到证明；英语首见通常定为十六世纪三十年代，但只是约数。

note.en: Group one holds words that resemble humidity but belong to other roots; group two holds words for moisture itself.
note.cn: 第一组是外形像 humidity、却属于其他词根的词；第二组是表示潮湿本身的词。

entries.definition: From Latin humilis 'low, humble', from humus 'earth': the quality of being humble. The resemblance to humidity is accidental.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 humilis「低微的、谦卑的」，源于 humus「土地」：谦逊的品质。与 humidity 相似纯属偶然。

entries.definition: Dark organic matter in soil, from Latin humus 'earth'; it is a solid, not water vapour.
entries.definitionCN: 土壤中的深色有机质，来自拉丁 humus「土地」；它是固体，不是水汽。

entries.definition: To add water vapour to the air; it acts on air rather than naming the amount in it.
entries.definitionCN: 向空气加入水汽；作用于空气，而非指其中的数量。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning damp; humidity is the noun for the quantity or quality.
entries.definitionCN: 表示潮湿的形容词；humidity 是表示数量或性质的名词。

entries.definition: Water present in small amounts in air or a material; it names the water, while humidity names the amount in air.
entries.definitionCN: 空气或材料中少量存在的水；它指水本身，humidity 指空气中的含量。

entries.definition: The unpleasant quality of being slightly wet; it is closer to the felt side of humidity.
entries.definitionCN: 轻微潮湿的令人不适的性质；更接近 humidity 的体感一面。

entries.definition: Warm, humid air that feels oppressive; it combines heat with humidity.
entries.definitionCN: 闷热潮湿、令人压抑的空气；把热与湿度合在一起。

entries.definition: Water in its gaseous state; humidity is the measure of how much of it the air holds.
entries.definitionCN: 气态的水；humidity 是空气含有多少这种水的度量。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real word parts, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin humere 'to be moist' gives humid, humidity, humidify.
normal.cn: 拉丁 humere「潮湿」给出 humid、humidity、humidify。

normal.en: The family runs humidity, humid, humidify, humidifier, dehumidify.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 humidity、humid、humidify、humidifier、dehumidify。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the measures: relative humidity, absolute humidity, specific humidity.
normal.cn: 固定搭配区分度量：相对湿度、绝对湿度、比湿。

normal.en: Weather reports usually mean relative humidity when they say humidity.
normal.cn: 天气报告说 humidity 时通常指相对湿度。

normal.en: The trap is humility, from humus 'earth', which means modesty.
normal.cn: 陷阱是 humility，出自 humus「土地」，意为谦逊。

abstract.en: Picture a towel on a wall that never dries.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上一条永远不干的毛巾。

abstract.en: Picture a window fogged from the inside in the afternoon.
abstract.cn: 想象午后窗玻璃从内侧蒙上雾。

abstract.en: Picture air holding water the way a sponge holds it, until warmth makes it let go.
abstract.cn: 想象空气像海绵一样含水，直到温度让它松开。

examples.en: Humidity above eighty per cent slows the drying of paint.
examples.cn: 湿度超过八成会拖慢油漆干燥。

examples.en: The instrument logs temperature and humidity every hour.
examples.cn: 仪器每小时记录温度与湿度。

examples.en: Low humidity in winter can dry out the throat.
examples.cn: 冬季低湿度会让喉咙干燥。

dict_mnemonic.text: humid 是潮湿的，-ity 是名词后缀：潮湿的程度 → 湿度；气象上说「湿度」多半指相对湿度，别与谦逊 humility 混了

root: 拉丁 humere「潮湿」→ humidus「潮湿的」→ humiditas「潮湿」→ 英语 humidity；更深印欧词根属重构形式，来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one measured moisture: the vapour in the air, the relative and absolute measures, the per-mass measure, the felt stickiness, the weather figure, the indoor target and the effects on materials and bodies.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种可测的水汽展开：空气中的水汽、相对与绝对两种度量、按质量计的度量、体感的黏湿、天气报告的数值、室内的目标值，以及对材料与人体的影响。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a towel on a wall that never dries.
core.cn: 核心意象：墙上一条永远不干的毛巾。

branches.en: THE SUBSTANCE: the word first names vapour held in the air.
branches.cn: 物质：这个词首先指空气中持有的水汽。

branches.en: THREE MEASURES: relative to capacity, absolute by volume, specific by mass.
branches.cn: 三种度量：相对容量、按体积的绝对量、按质量的比湿。

branches.en: THE FEELING: the same quantity is felt on the skin as stickiness.
branches.cn: 体感：同一个量在皮肤上被感受为黏湿。

branches.en: THE FIGURE: the forecast prints the quantity beside the temperature.
branches.cn: 数值：预报把这个量与温度并列印出。

branches.en: CONTROL AND CONSEQUENCE: museums hold it steady, and materials pay the price when it is not held.
branches.cn: 控制与后果：博物馆让它稳定，若不稳定材料就要付代价。

intro.en: Humidity is a Latin noun with a Latin adjective inside it, and that adjective also builds the verbs for adding and removing moisture.
intro.cn: humidity 是一个拉丁名词，里面藏着一个拉丁形容词，那个形容词还构成加湿与除湿的动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin humere, humidus and humiditas supply the core, and English adds -ify for the action of making air moist.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 humere、humidus 与 humiditas 提供核心，英语再加 -ify 表示使空气变湿的动作。

items.example: The verb names the state behind the noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指名词背后的状态。

items.example: The adjective describes the air.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述空气。

items.example: The suffix turns the adjective into a noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成名词。

items.example: Humidity stayed high all week.
items.exampleCN: 湿度整周居高不下。

items.example: The air felt humid in the shade.
items.exampleCN: 阴凉处的空气也显得潮湿。

items.meaning: to add vapour to the air
items.example: The machine humidifies the greenhouse.
items.exampleCN: 这台机器为温室加湿。

items.example: A humidifier ran beside the bed.
items.exampleCN: 床边开着加湿器。

items.meaning: to take vapour out of the air
items.example: The cellar must be dehumidified.
items.exampleCN: 地窖必须除湿。

items.example: A hygrometer hung by the window.
items.exampleCN: 窗边挂着一只湿度计。

definition_zh: adj. 可扣除的；可减去的 n.（保险）免赔额；自付额
definition_en: that can be taken away from a total, especially from tax; as a noun, the amount you pay before insurance covers the rest

scene: 这笔开支是可以抵税的。 The expense is deductible from tax.

pos.zh: 可扣除的；可减去的
（保险）免赔额；自付额

senses.title: Allowed against tax
senses.definition: that may be taken away from taxable income
senses.definitionCN: 可以从应税收入中减去的
senses.example: The expense is deductible from tax.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔开支可以抵税。
senses.why: A column marked as removable on a tax form.
senses.whyCN: 税表上被标为可去掉的一栏。

senses.title: Allowed from any total
senses.definition: that may be taken away from any total or score
senses.definitionCN: 可以从任何总额或分数中减去的
senses.example: The fee is deductible from the final bill.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔费用可从最终账单中扣除。
senses.why: A line the rules allow you to cross out.
senses.whyCN: 规则允许你划掉的一行。

senses.title: The part you pay first
senses.definition: the amount you pay yourself before insurance pays
senses.definitionCN: 保险赔付之前由你自己承担的金额
senses.example: The policy has a deductible of five hundred.
senses.exampleCN: 这份保单有五百的免赔额。
senses.why: A threshold the insurer will not cross.
senses.whyCN: 一道保险公司不肯跨过的门槛。

intro.en: Deductible is deduct plus -ible, from Latin deducere, to lead away.
intro.cn: deductible 由 deduct 加 -ible 构成，deduct 源自拉丁语 deducere（领走）。

items.en: Ducere meant to lead.
items.cn: ducere 意为引领。

items.en: Deducere meant to lead away.
items.cn: deducere 意为领走。

items.en: Deduct entered English for taking an amount away.
items.cn: 十五世纪 deduct 以扣除数额义进入英语。

items.en: Deductible was formed with the able suffix.
items.cn: 十七世纪 deductible 加上「可以」后缀构成。

items.en: Deductible became standard in tax rules.
items.cn: 二十世纪 deductible 成为税务规则的标准词。

items.en: Deductible also names the insurance excess.
items.cn: 如今 deductible 也指保险的免赔额。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the duct- family; the near-meaning group names what may be taken off.
note.cn: 形近组同属 duct- 家族；近义组都是「可以减掉」的说法。

entries.definition: Able to be worked out by reasoning.
entries.definitionCN: 可推断的。

entries.definition: Able to be made smaller or simpler.
entries.definitionCN: 可减小的；可简化的。

entries.definition: Of reasoning from examples to a general rule.
entries.definitionCN: 归纳的。

entries.definition: Allowed by rules or law.
entries.definitionCN: 允许的；可容许的。

entries.definition: Not required to pay or do something.
entries.definitionCN: 豁免的。

entries.definition: On which tax must be paid.
entries.definitionCN: 应税的。

entries.definition: The amount you pay before insurance covers.
entries.definitionCN: 免赔额；自付部分。

normalIntro.en: Deductible is deduct plus -ible: able to be led away from the total.
normalIntro.cn: deductible 就是 deduct 加 -ible：可以从总额里被领走的。

normal.en: Deduct means to take away.
normal.cn: deduct 意为扣除。

normal.en: The suffix -ible means able to be.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ible 意为可以被。

normal.en: Deductible can be taken off.
normal.cn: deductible 是可以被减掉的。

normal.en: Tax forms list deductible items.
normal.cn: 税表列出可扣除的项目。

normal.en: Insurance asks for a deductible first.
normal.cn: 保险先要你付免赔额。

abstract.en: A column marked as removable on a tax form.
abstract.cn: 税表上被标为可去掉的一栏。

abstract.en: A line the rules allow you to cross out.

abstract.cn: 一道保险公司不肯跨过的门槛。

examples.en: Charity gifts are tax deductible here.
examples.cn: 在这里慈善捐赠可以抵税。

examples.en: The deductible on this policy is quite low.
examples.cn: 这份保单的免赔额相当低。

examples.en: Keep receipts for every deductible expense.
examples.cn: 保留每一笔可扣除开支的收据。

dict_mnemonic.text: deductible 谐音「弟大克特博」——不如记 deduct（扣除）＋ ible（可以）＝「可以被扣掉的」，税务上指可抵税，保险上指自付额。

sensesIntro.en: One removable line: against tax, against a bill, and the part you pay.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一道可去掉的线：抵税、抵账单，以及你自己付的那一段。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a column on a form marked as removable, and a threshold you must cross yourself
core.cn: 核心意象：表格上被标为可去掉的一栏，以及一道必须自己跨过的门槛

branches.en: A column marked as removable on a tax form.
branches.cn: 税表上被标为可去掉的一栏。

branches.cn: 两者都指规则允许你减掉的部分。

branches.en: Both are a share of a total kept apart from the rest.
branches.cn: 两者都是从总额中单独划出来的一份。

definition_zh: 现代主义；现代思潮；艺术、文学与音乐中反叛旧形式、试验新形式的运动；宗教现代主义
definition_en: a movement in art, literature, music and thought that rejected inherited rules and experimented with new forms
core_image: 一间白墙展厅里，旧画框被逐一取下，画布上只剩下不肯对齐的色块与断裂的线条
scene: 二十世纪初的画廊里，评论家在一幅打碎透视的油画前停下脚步， The gallery's new wing is devoted to modernism, with canvases that abandon perspective.
sceneCN: 这里 modernism 指「十九世纪末至二十世纪中叶反叛旧形式、试验新形式的艺术运动」（第 1 个义项：美术、文学与音乐中的自觉运动）；句意为画廊新翼专门陈列现代主义作品，画布上放弃了透视法。图中可辨识物件：白墙展厅、歪斜的画框、断裂的色块、评论家的笔记本。

pos.zh: 现代主义（艺术、文学、音乐运动）；现代思潮；宗教现代主义
