senses.title: An artistic movement that broke with inherited forms
senses.titleCN: 打破旧形式的艺术运动
senses.definition: a late nineteenth and early twentieth century movement in art, literature and music that rejected established rules and experimented with new forms
senses.definitionCN: 十九世纪末至二十世纪初在美术、文学与音乐中拒绝既定规则、试验新形式的运动
senses.example: Modernism in painting abandoned perspective and told stories without a plot.
senses.exampleCN: 绘画中的现代主义放弃了透视法，也不按情节讲故事。
senses.why: The label names a deliberate break: artists treated the rules they inherited as something to dismantle, so the movement is defined by its refusal of the old rather than by one shared style.
senses.whyCN: 这个词标记的是一次有意的断裂：艺术家把继承来的规则当作要拆掉的东西，因此这场运动由「拒绝旧法」来定义，而不是由某一种统一风格来定义。

senses.title: The wider modern outlook
senses.titleCN: 更广义的现代思想倾向
senses.definition: the outlook that trusts reason, progress and the present age rather than inherited authority
senses.definitionCN: 信任理性、进步与当下时代、而非继承来的权威的思想倾向
senses.example: Modernism in philosophy placed reason above revelation.
senses.exampleCN: 哲学中的现代主义把理性置于启示之上。
senses.why: Once the label moved from studios to thought, it named not a style but a stance: the present is trusted to judge the past.
senses.whyCN: 当这个词从画室移到思想领域，它指的不再是风格，而是一种立场：让当下有权审判过去。

senses.title: Religious modernism
senses.definition: a movement that reinterpreted religious doctrine in the light of modern scholarship and science
senses.definitionCN: 依据现代学术与科学重新解释宗教教义的运动
senses.example: Catholic modernism was condemned by the church in the early twentieth century.
senses.exampleCN: 天主教现代主义在二十世纪初遭到教会谴责。
senses.why: Here the break with the past happens inside a faith: old doctrine is kept but read through modern methods, which is why the label could be both a programme and an accusation.
senses.whyCN: 这里的断裂发生在信仰内部：旧教义被保留，却要用现代方法去读，因此这个标签既可以是纲领，也可以是一项罪名。

senses.title: Modernism in architecture
senses.definition: a style of building that strips away ornament and lets function and new materials shape the form
senses.definitionCN: 去除装饰、让功能与新材料决定形体的建筑风格
senses.example: Modernism in architecture gave the library a flat roof and a glass wall.
senses.exampleCN: 建筑中的现代主义给图书馆装上了平屋顶与玻璃墙。
senses.why: The same refusal of inherited rules becomes physical: ornament is treated as a lie, and structure is left visible.
senses.whyCN: 同样是对继承规则的拒绝，这次落到实体上：装饰被视为谎言，结构则被露出来。

senses.title: Literary modernism
senses.definition: the literary practice of breaking narrative order, mixing voices and testing the limits of language
senses.definitionCN: 打破叙事顺序、混合多种声音并试探语言边界的小说与诗歌实践
senses.example: Modernism in fiction replaced the omniscient narrator with fractured inner voices.
senses.exampleCN: 小说中的现代主义用破碎的内心声音取代了全知叙述者。
senses.why: If the old novel assumed one orderly observer, modernism assumes many partial minds, so the text itself becomes fragmented.
senses.whyCN: 旧小说假定有一个整齐的观察者，现代主义则假定有许多片面的心灵，于是文本本身也碎裂开来。

senses.title: Modernism in music
senses.definition: the musical search for new scales, dissonance and rhythm after the breakdown of traditional tonality
senses.definitionCN: 传统调性瓦解后，对音阶、不协和音与节奏的新探索
senses.example: Modernism in music dissolved the key signature into pure rhythm.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐中的现代主义把调号消解成纯粹的节奏。
senses.why: Music shows the break most sharply: the shared grammar of key is abandoned, and each work must build its own rules.
senses.whyCN: 音乐把这种断裂表现得最尖锐：共同的调性语法被放弃，每部作品都得自己造一套规则。

senses.title: A period label used by critics
senses.titleCN: 评论家使用的时期标签
senses.definition: a label applied by critics and curators to the art of a particular period or group
senses.definitionCN: 评论家与策展人用来指某一时期或某一群体艺术的标签
senses.example: The curator dates the modernism of the group to the years just before the war.
senses.exampleCN: 策展人把这个团体的现代主义定在战前那几年。
senses.why: A movement needs a name before it can be taught, so modernism also works as a period label that gathers scattered works under one heading.
senses.whyCN: 一场运动要先有名字才能被讲授，因此现代主义也充当时期标签，把散落的作品收在同一个标题下。

senses.title: A preference for whatever is new
senses.titleCN: 一味求新的偏好（常含贬义）
senses.definition: a liking for new things simply because they are new, often used with disapproval
senses.definitionCN: 只因事物新就喜欢它，常用于贬义
senses.example: The mayor's modernism consists of replacing every old bench with a steel one.
senses.exampleCN: 这位市长的现代主义就是把每条旧长椅都换成钢制的。
senses.why: The positive demand to break with dead rules can harden into a reflex that treats age itself as a fault, and this sense names that reflex.
senses.whyCN: 原本积极的「打破死规则」会硬化成一种条件反射，把「旧」本身当成缺点，这个义项指的就是这种反射。

intro.en: Modernism joins the Late Latin adjective modernus with the movement-naming suffix -ism. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: modernism 由晚期拉丁语形容词 modernus 与表示「主义、运动」的后缀结合而成。年代均为约数。

items.en: The adverb modo meant just now, recently. It is usually explained as a form built on modus, measure or manner, and that link is a standard account rather than a recorded certainty.
items.cn: 副词 modo 意为「刚刚、近来」。通行解释认为它由表示「尺度、方式」的 modus 变来，但这只是标准说法，并非有记录的确证。

items.en: Late Latin modernus, of the present time, was formed from that time word plus the adjective ending -nus. It contrasted the present age with the older past.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 modernus 意为「当下的、此刻的」，由这个时间词加形容词词尾 -nus 构成，用来把当下时代与更早的过去对照。

items.en: The suffix -ismus in Latin came from Greek -ismos, which named a practice, doctrine or movement. English -ism entered through French and Latin and became highly productive.
items.cn: 拉丁语后缀 -ismus 来自希腊语 -ismos，用来指某种实践、学说或运动。英语的 -ism 经法语与拉丁语进入，后来极能产。

items.en: French modernisme appeared in the nineteenth century, first in religious controversy and then in discussion of the arts.
items.cn: 法语 modernisme 在十九世纪出现，先用于宗教争论，随后进入艺术讨论。

items.en: English adopted modernism in the early twentieth century as a name for self-conscious experimental art, and critics soon extended it to architecture, music and literature.
items.cn: 英语在二十世纪初引入 modernism，用来命名自觉试验新形式的艺术，评论家很快又把它扩展到建筑、音乐与文学。

items.en: Source uncertain: reference works date the first English artistic use differently, and the religious sense was fixed only after the church condemnation, so exact first citations should be treated as doubtful.
items.cn: 来源不确定：各家参考资料对英语中艺术义的首见年代说法不一；宗教义是在教会谴责之后才固定下来的，因此确切的首见书证应视为存疑。

note.en: The first group holds words from the same modern- stock that differ in word class or reference; the second holds art movements that are often set beside modernism.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 modern- 词干、但词性或所指不同的词；第二组是常被拿来与现代主义并列讨论的艺术运动。

entries.definition: The state or experience of living in a modern age; it names a condition, while modernism names a movement that responds to that condition.
entries.definitionCN: 生活在现代时代的处境或体验；它指一种状态，而现代主义指回应这种状态的运动。

entries.definition: Belonging to the present age or to a recent style; the adjective can describe anything current, while modernism is a named movement.
entries.definitionCN: 属于当下时代或较近风格的；这个形容词可描述任何当下事物，而现代主义是有名的运动。

entries.definition: To make something modern in equipment, method or design; modernism is the cultural movement, not the act of upgrading.
entries.definitionCN: 在设备、方法或设计上使某物现代化；现代主义是文化运动，不是升级改造的动作。

entries.definition: The process of becoming industrial, urban and technically up to date; it is a social and economic process, not an artistic programme.
entries.definitionCN: 走向工业化、城市化与技术更新的过程；这是社会与经济过程，不是艺术纲领。

entries.definition: A later reaction that mixes styles, doubts grand narratives and often quotes modernism ironically.
entries.definitionCN: 后来的反拨：混合风格、怀疑宏大叙事，并常带反讽地引用现代主义。

entries.definition: The artists who lead experimental practice; modernism is the broader movement, while the avant-garde names its most forward and provocative wing.
entries.definitionCN: 引领实验性创作的艺术家群体；现代主义是更宽的运动，先锋派指它最前卫、最具挑衅性的一翼。

entries.definition: A movement that aims to show ordinary life as it is; modernism often defines itself against realism even when it keeps realistic detail.
entries.definitionCN: 力求如实呈现日常生活的运动；现代主义常靠反对写实主义来定义自己，即便仍保留写实细节。

entries.definition: Adherence to the balanced rules and models of ancient art; it is the inherited standard that modernism set out to break.
entries.definitionCN: 遵奉古代艺术均衡规则与范本的立场；它正是现代主义要打破的继承标准。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real suffix, the real word family and the phrases the word actually keeps.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的后缀、真实的同族词，以及这个词实际常用的搭配。

normal.en: modern plus the movement suffix: the same suffix builds realism and socialism, so it names a programme rather than a single object.
normal.cn: modern 加上表示「主义、运动」的后缀：同类后缀也构成 realism（写实主义）与 socialism（社会主义），所以它命名的是一套纲领，而不是单个物件。

normal.en: The family runs modern, modernist, modernistic, modernize, modernization and modernity.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 modern（现代的）、modernist（现代主义者）、modernistic（带现代主义色彩的）、modernize（使现代化）、modernization（现代化）、modernity（现代性）。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the fields: modernism in art, architectural modernism, literary modernism, religious modernism.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：艺术中的现代主义、建筑现代主义、文学现代主义、宗教现代主义。

normal.en: The movement is dated by manifestos and exhibitions rather than by one invention.
normal.cn: 这场运动的年代靠宣言与展览来定，而不是靠某一项发明。

normal.en: In art history its usual opposite is classicism or realism, not simply age.
normal.cn: 在艺术史里，它通常的对立面是古典主义或写实主义，而不只是「年长」。

abstract.en: Picture a gallery where every frame has been taken down and the wall itself becomes the work.
abstract.cn: 想象一间画廊，所有画框都被取下，墙面本身成了作品。

abstract.en: Picture a stone column replaced by a glass box that carries the same weight.
abstract.cn: 想象一根石柱被一只承受同样重量的玻璃盒取代。

abstract.en: Picture a clock whose hands point only forward, refusing to measure the past.
abstract.cn: 想象一只指针只朝前走的钟，拒绝丈量过去。

examples.en: Modernism in poetry broke the line and let the sentence spill across the page.
examples.cn: 诗歌中的现代主义打断了诗行，让句子漫过页面。

examples.en: The exhibition traces modernism from its first manifestos to its late echoes.
examples.cn: 展览追溯现代主义从最初宣言到晚期回声的历程。

examples.en: Critics accused the architect of modernism for removing every ornament from the church.
examples.cn: 评论家指责这位建筑师把教堂的所有装饰都去掉，是十足的现代主义。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「摩登主义」——把「摩登」（时髦）加「主义」，就是一味求新、反叛旧形式的现代主义。

root: 由晚期拉丁语 modernus「当下的、此刻的」加表示「主义、运动」的后缀构成。modernus 通行说法追溯至 modo「刚刚、近来」，而 modo 又常被解释为由 modus「尺度、方式」变来；这两层联系属标准说法，并非有记录的确证。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one break: inherited rules are refused, and that refusal is applied to painting, thought, faith, buildings, fiction, music, period labels and finally to mere novelty.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次断裂展开：先拒绝继承来的规则，再把这次拒绝依次用于绘画、思想、信仰、建筑、小说、音乐、时期标签，最后滑向单纯的求新。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a frame taken off the wall so that the canvas can set its own rules.
core.cn: 核心意象：画框被从墙上取下，好让画布自己定规则。

branches.en: MOVEMENT AND OUTLOOK: the artistic break hardens into a general trust in reason, progress and the present.
branches.cn: 运动与思想倾向：艺术上的断裂硬化成对理性、进步与当下的普遍信任。

branches.en: FAITH RECAST: the same modern method is turned inward on religious doctrine.
branches.cn: 重释信仰：同一套现代方法被转向宗教教义内部。

branches.en: BARE STRUCTURE: ornament is refused so that function and material can speak.
branches.cn: 裸露结构：拒绝装饰，让功能与材料自己说话。

branches.en: FRAGMENTED VOICE AND SOUND: fiction splits into many minds, and music gives up the shared key.
branches.cn: 碎裂的声音与声响：小说分裂成许多心灵，音乐则放弃共同的调性。

branches.en: LABEL AND REFLEX: critics turn the break into a period name, and the name can decay into a reflex of liking only what is new.
branches.cn: 标签与反射：评论家把这次断裂变成时期名称，而这个名称又会退化为「只爱新东西」的条件反射。

intro.en: Modernism can be read from a time word, a Latin adjective ending and a movement-naming suffix.
intro.cn: modernism 可以按一个时间词、一个拉丁形容词词尾与一个表示运动的后缀逐段读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin modus and modo supply the time sense, modernus turns it into an adjective, and the suffix from Greek -ismos turns the adjective into a named movement.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 modus 与 modo 提供时间含义，modernus 把它变成形容词，来自希腊语 -ismos 的后缀再把形容词变成有名目的运动。

items.example: The stem also appears in mode and modest.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干也出现在 mode（方式）与 modest（适度的）里。

items.example: The adjective entered English through French in the sixteenth century.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词在十六世纪经法语进入英语。

items.structure: -ism (suffix naming a practice, doctrine or movement)
items.example: The same ending builds realism and socialism.
items.exampleCN: 同一后缀也构成 realism（写实主义）与 socialism（社会主义）。

items.meaning: an artist or thinker who works in the modern style
items.meaningCN: 以现代风格创作的艺术家或思想家
items.example: The modernist trusted the new materials of the age.
items.exampleCN: 这位现代主义者信任那个时代的新材料。

items.meaning: marked by the manner of modernism
items.example: The lobby has a modernistic glass ceiling.
items.exampleCN: 大堂有一片现代主义风格的玻璃顶。

items.meaning: to make modern in method or equipment
items.meaningCN: 在方法或设备上使现代化
items.example: The mill modernized its looms.
items.exampleCN: 磨坊把织机现代化了。

items.example: Modernization changed the harbour within a decade.
items.exampleCN: 现代化在十年内改变了这座港口。

items.example: The novel is a study of urban modernity.
items.exampleCN: 这部小说研究的是城市现代性。

items.meaning: a later movement that reacts against modernism
items.meaningCN: 后来反拨现代主义的运动
items.example: Postmodernism quotes the old styles with irony.
items.exampleCN: 后现代主义带着反讽引用旧风格。

derivatives.meaning: several varieties or periods of modernism
derivatives.meaningCN: 现代主义的多种形态或时期
以带现代主义色彩的方式

definition_zh: 自治的；自主的；有自主权的；自行运转的；（车辆、机器）无人驾驶的、自主运行的
definition_en: governing itself or acting on its own, without control from outside, including machines that operate without a driver
core_image: 一辆没有驾驶座的车在田垄间自己转弯，方向盘转得比人手还稳
scene: 拖拉机沿着垄沟自己走，遇到地头的石堆就减速绕开，驾驶室里空着。 An autonomous tractor steers itself across the field and slows for the stones at the edge.
sceneCN: 这里指机器无人驾驶、自行作业（第 4 个义项：无人驾驶的、自主运行的）；句意为这台无人驾驶的拖拉机自己穿过田地，遇到地边的石堆就减速。场景图取象：一辆没有驾驶座的车在田垄间自己转弯。

pos.zh: 自治的；自主的（地区、机构）
自主行动的；不受外部支配的（人、决定）
（车辆、机器）无人驾驶的；自主运行的
（哲学、伦理）自律的；自我立法的

derivatives.zh: 自治；自主权（把希腊语「自己的」与「法、规矩」合在一起，字面即「自己的法」）
自主地；自行地（加副词词尾，指不受外部操控地运行）
自主神经的；自动调节的（同源形容词，现代医学多用来指不受意识支配的神经系统）
自治主义（加表示「学说、倾向」的后缀）
使自治；使自主（加表示「使成为」的动词词尾）
自治主义者；主张自主者（加表示「从事者、主张者」的名词后缀）

senses.title: Self-governing in law
senses.definition: of a region, institution or community, having the right to govern its own affairs
senses.definitionCN: 指地区、机构或群体有权管理自身事务
senses.example: The autonomous region sets its own school curriculum.
senses.exampleCN: 这个自治区自行制定学校课程。
senses.why: The Greek word literally means living under one's own law, so self-rule is its oldest sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个希腊词字面就是按自己的法生活，因此自治是最古老的义项。

senses.title: Acting independently
senses.definition: able to act or decide without direction from another person or body
senses.definitionCN: 无需他人或他机构指示即可行动或决定
senses.example: The research unit is autonomous in how it spends its grant.
senses.exampleCN: 这个研究单位在如何使用经费上自主。
senses.why: From self-rule in law the word moved to self-direction in ordinary institutions.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从法律上的自治，转到一般机构里的自行其是。

senses.title: Self-directed as a person
senses.definition: of a person, able to think and choose for oneself rather than being led
senses.definitionCN: 指人能独立思考和选择，而非被人牵着走
senses.example: An autonomous learner asks the next question without being told.
senses.exampleCN: 自主的学习者不用别人吩咐就会问下一个问题。
senses.why: Education and ethics both prize the person who can set a rule for himself.
senses.whyCN: 教育与伦理都看重那个能替自己立规矩的人。

senses.title: Driverless in the physical world
senses.definition: of a vehicle or machine, able to move and operate without a human driver
senses.definitionCN: 指车辆或机器无需人驾驶即可移动与作业
senses.example: An autonomous tractor steers itself across the field and slows for the stones at the edge.
senses.exampleCN: 这台无人驾驶的拖拉机自己穿过田地，遇到地边的石堆就减速。
senses.why: A machine that needs no hand on the wheel is self-governing in the most literal way.
senses.whyCN: 不需要手扶方向盘的机器，是最字面意义上的自治者。

senses.title: A self-running system
senses.definition: of software or a system, able to monitor its own state and act without a human in the loop
senses.definitionCN: 指软件或系统能监测自身状态并在无人介入时行动
senses.example: The autonomous system rerouted traffic when the sensor failed.
senses.exampleCN: 传感器失效时，这套自主系统重新规划了车流。
senses.why: Computing took the word for loops that close on themselves, a small republic of code.
senses.whyCN: 计算机领域用这个词指自我闭合的循环，是一小块代码的自治体。

senses.title: Moral self-legislation
senses.definition: in philosophy, the capacity of a rational being to give itself its own moral law
senses.definitionCN: 在哲学中，指理性存在者替自己立下道德法则的能力
senses.example: Kant placed autonomy at the centre of moral worth.
senses.exampleCN: 康德把自律置于道德价值的中心。
senses.why: The Greek image of giving oneself a law became, in ethics, the ground of dignity.
senses.whyCN: 为自己立法的希腊意象，在伦理学里成了尊严的根据。

senses.title: A self-governing agent
senses.definition: in artificial intelligence, an agent that pursues goals without continuous instruction
senses.definitionCN: 在人工智能中，指无需持续指令即可追求目标的智能体
senses.example: The autonomous agent books the tickets and confirms them itself.
senses.exampleCN: 这个自主代理自己订票并自己确认。
senses.why: Software agents were named after political self-rule, a joke that became a technical term.
senses.whyCN: 软件代理借用了政治上的自治，这个玩笑后来成了技术术语。

senses.title: Weapons that choose
senses.definition: of a weapon system, able to select and engage targets without human decision
senses.definitionCN: 指武器系统能不经人决定就选择并攻击目标
senses.example: Talks on autonomous weapons stalled over the question of accountability.
senses.exampleCN: 关于自主武器的谈判卡在责任归属问题上。
senses.why: When the machine picks the target, the word stops being neutral and becomes a warning.
senses.whyCN: 当机器自己挑目标，这个词就不再中性，而成了警告。

senses.title: Not the same as automatic
senses.definition: governed by its own rules rather than merely following a fixed mechanical sequence
senses.definitionCN: 按自身规则行事，而不只是执行固定的机械序列
senses.example: A thermostat is automatic; a system that rewrites its own rules is autonomous.
senses.exampleCN: 恒温器是自动的；能改写自身规则的系统才是自主的。
senses.why: Automatic comes from a Greek word for acting of itself, but only autonomy implies law of one's own.
senses.whyCN: 「自动」出自希腊语「自行动作」，但只有「自主」才含有自己的法之意。

intro.en: Autonomous comes from Greek autonomos, 'living under one's own laws', from autos 'self' and nomos 'law or custom'. The formation is clear; the exact date of its English entry is uncertain.
intro.cn: autonomous 出自希腊语 autonomos「按自己的法生活」，由 autos「自己」与 nomos「法、习俗」构成。构词清楚，进入英语的确切年代不确定。

items.en: Autos meant self or the same, and it is the source of auto- in automatic, autobiography and automobile.
items.cn: autos 意为自身、同一，是 automatic、autobiography 与 automobile 中 auto- 的来源。

items.en: Nomos meant law, custom or usage, and it also stands behind economy, astronomy and taxonomy.
items.cn: nomos 意为法、习俗、惯例，economy、astronomy 与 taxonomy 也由它而来。

items.en: The compound described a city or people living under its own laws rather than under an outside ruler.
items.cn: 这个复合词描述按自己的法而非按外来统治者之法治生活的城邦或民族。

items.en: Greek politics made autonomy a claim of cities, and the word entered political argument before philosophy used it.
items.cn: 希腊政治使自治成为城邦的主张，这个词先进入政治论辩，后被哲学使用。

items.en: Kant gave autonomy a moral sense, the rational will legislating for itself, which is still the philosophical anchor.
items.cn: 康德赋予自律道德含义，即理性意志替自己立法，这仍是哲学上的锚点。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word was applied to vehicles and software, extending self-rule from cities to machines.
items.cn: 二十世纪，这个词被用于车辆与软件，把自治从城邦扩展到机器。

note.en: The first group shares the self or law root or looks close; the second group holds the related words that are routinely confused with autonomous.
note.cn: 第一组或共享「自己」或「法」的词根，或字形相近；第二组是常与 autonomous 混淆的相关词。

entries.definition: The noun: the right or condition of self-government.
entries.definitionCN: 名词：自治的权利或状态。

entries.definition: The adverb for acting without outside control.
entries.definitionCN: 副词：不受外部控制地行动。

entries.definition: Of the nervous system that regulates the body without conscious control.
entries.definitionCN: 指不受意识支配、自行调节身体的神经系统。

entries.definition: Working by itself mechanically; it shares autos but its second half means acting of itself, not law.
entries.definitionCN: 机械地自行工作；共享「自己」，后半却意为自行动作而非法。

entries.definition: Nameless; it looks close but comes from a word meaning name.
entries.definitionCN: 无名的；字形相近，却出自意为「名字」的词。

entries.definition: Not controlled by another, the everyday word for the same idea.
entries.definitionCN: 不受他人控制，是同一意思的日常说法。

entries.definition: Ruling itself, the plain English equivalent of the political sense.
entries.definitionCN: 自我治理，是政治义项最朴素的英语对应。

entries.definition: Without a human driver, the narrow transport sense.
entries.definitionCN: 无人类驾驶，是交通领域的窄义。

entries.definition: Holding supreme authority, stronger and more legal than autonomous.
entries.definitionCN: 握有最高权力，比 autonomous 更强、更法律化。

entries.definition: Setting one's own course, the personal sense without the legal weight.
entries.definitionCN: 自己定方向，是个人层面的意思，没有法律分量。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real self and law roots, the real family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「自己」与「法」词根、真实词族与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: Autos is self and nomos is law, so autonomous means living under one's own law.
normal.cn: 前者是自己，后者是法，合起来就是按自己的法生活。

normal.en: The family runs autonomy, autonomous, autonomously, autonomic and autonomism.
normal.cn: 同族词有 autonomy、autonomous、autonomously、autonomic 与 autonomism。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: autonomous region, autonomous vehicle, autonomous system, autonomous learning.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出用法：自治区、无人驾驶车辆、自主系统、自主学习。

normal.en: The word has three lines: a region governs itself, a person directs himself, a machine drives itself.
normal.cn: 这个词有三条线：地区自治、个人自主、机器自驾。

normal.en: Keep it apart from automatic, which only means working by itself.
normal.cn: 要与「自动」分开，后者只是自行工作。

abstract.en: Autonomy is not the absence of rules but the presence of one's own.
abstract.cn: 自主不是没有规则，而是有一套自己的规则。

abstract.en: A machine that governs itself raises the oldest political question in a new body.
abstract.cn: 自行治理的机器，把最古老的政治问题装进了一具新的身体。

abstract.en: Self-rule is a burden before it is a freedom.
abstract.cn: 自治先是负担，然后才是自由。

examples.en: The province became autonomous after the treaty.
examples.cn: 条约签订后，这个省取得自治。

examples.en: Autonomous vehicles still struggle with unmapped roads.
examples.cn: 无人驾驶车辆在未测绘的道路上仍吃力。

examples.en: She encouraged autonomous work rather than close supervision.
examples.cn: 她鼓励自主工作，而不是紧盯着管。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「奥托诺默斯」——自己给自己定规矩，自己走自己的路：自治的、自主的

root: 希腊语 autonomos「按自己的法生活」← autos「自己」＋ nomos「法、习俗」；nomos 另见于 economy、astronomy、taxonomy。政治义先出，康德赋予道德自律义，二十世纪扩展到无人驾驶车辆与自主软件系统。进入英语确切年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one self-made law: a self-governing region, an independent institution, a self-directed person, a driverless machine, a self-running system, moral self-legislation, a software agent, a weapon that chooses, and the contrast with merely automatic.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿着同一部自订的法：自治地区、独立机构、自主的个人、无人驾驶的机器、自行运转的系统、道德的自我立法、软件智能体、自行选择的武器，以及与「自动」的区别。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tractor with an empty cab turning a corner by itself, steadier than a human hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：空着驾驶室的拖拉机自己转过弯来，比人手还稳。

branches.en: THE GOVERNING BODY: a region or institution that sets its own rules and spends its own budget.
branches.cn: 治理的主体：自订规则、自支预算的地区或机构。

branches.en: THE SELF-LEGISLATING PERSON: a learner who asks the next question, and a will that gives itself a moral law.
branches.cn: 自我立法的个人：自己问出下一个问题的学习者，以及替自己立道德法的意志。

branches.en: THE MACHINE THAT RUNS ITSELF: a driverless tractor, and software that acts with no hand in the loop.
branches.cn: 自行运转的机器：无人驾驶的拖拉机，以及无人介入即行动的软件。

branches.en: THE AGENT AND THE WEAPON: a program pursuing a goal, and a system that picks its own target.
branches.cn: 智能体与武器：追求目标的程序，以及自己挑选目标的系统。

branches.en: THE DISTINCTION: automatic follows a fixed sequence; autonomous follows a law of its own.
branches.cn: 那条区别：自动执行固定序列，自主遵循自己的法。

intro.en: Autonomous is a Greek compound of self and law, with a family that runs from politics through philosophy into robotics.
intro.cn: autonomous 是「自己」与「法」的希腊复合词，其词族从政治经哲学一直延伸到机器人技术。

latinIntro.en: The source is Greek rather than Latin: autos and nomos, with the adjective ending -os becoming -ous in English.
latinIntro.cn: 来源是希腊语而非拉丁语：autos 与 nomos，形容词词尾 -os 在英语中变成 -ous。

items.example: The adjective covers regions, persons and machines.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词覆盖地区、个人与机器。

items.example: It supplies the auto- in many English words.
items.exampleCN: 它提供许多英语词里的 auto-。

items.example: It also stands behind economy and astronomy.
items.exampleCN: economy 与 astronomy 也由它而来。

items.example: The noun names the condition rather than the holder.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指状态而非持有者。

items.example: It builds autonomous, famous and dangerous.
items.exampleCN: 它构成自治的、著名的与危险的等词。

items.example: It builds autonomously, meaning without outside control.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 autonomously，意为不受外部控制。

items.example: It builds autonomic, the medical adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 autonomic，即医学形容词。

items.example: It builds autonomism, a political stance.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 autonomism，一种政治立场。

items.example: It builds autonomize, to make self-governing.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 autonomize，意为使自治。

latinEntries.example: Greek autonomos means living under one's own law.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 希腊语 autonomos 意为按自己的法生活。

latinEntries.example: Greek autos means self, and gives the auto- of English.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 希腊语 autos 意为自己，并给出英语的 auto-。

latinEntries.example: Greek nomos means law or custom, and gives -nomy in English.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 希腊语 nomos 意为法、习俗，并给出英语的 -nomy。

definition_zh: 保留；保持；留存；记忆力；留任；潴留；保留金；所有权保留
definition_en: the act of keeping or holding something, whether information, people, fluid, or legal title
core_image: 一只手掌半握着一把湿沙，指缝间漏下的少，掌心里留下的多。
scene: 培训师在课后一周又发了同一份小测，发现大多数人都还记得那些术语，说明这次培训的内容留住了。 A week after the course, most trainees still remembered the terms, a sign of strong retention.
sceneCN: 这里 retention 是“所学内容的保持”（第 1 个义项）；句意：一周后多数人仍记得术语，说明知识被保持住了。

pos.zh: 保留；保持；留任；记忆力；潴留

senses.title: Knowledge staying put
senses.titleCN: 记忆保持：学过的东西留在脑中
senses.definition: the ability to keep information in memory over time
senses.definitionCN: 把信息在记忆中保留一段时间的能力
senses.example: Spaced practice improves retention more than rereading does.
senses.exampleCN: 间隔练习比反复阅读更能提高记忆保持。
senses.why: Retention comes from retinere, to hold back; what is learned is held, and forgetting is measured by how much escaped.
senses.whyCN: retention 出自 retinere“握紧不放”；学到的东西被握住，遗忘则用“漏掉了多少”来衡量。

senses.title: Keeping staff
senses.titleCN: 员工留任：组织把人留住
senses.definition: the proportion of employees who stay with an organisation over a period
senses.definitionCN: 一段时间内留在某机构的员工比例
senses.example: The company raised pay to improve staff retention.
senses.exampleCN: 公司提高薪酬以改善员工留任率。
senses.why: An organisation holds people the way a hand holds sand; retention statistics count those who did not slip away.
senses.whyCN: 组织留人如同手握沙；留任统计计的是没有漏走的人。

senses.title: Keeping records
senses.titleCN: 记录留存：按法规把文件保存一段时间
senses.definition: the practice of keeping documents or data for a required period
senses.definitionCN: 按规定期限保存文件或数据的做法
senses.example: The hospital follows a ten-year records retention policy.
senses.exampleCN: 这家医院执行十年记录留存政策。
senses.why: Here the held object is paper or data, and the holding is an obligation rather than a memory.
senses.whyCN: 这里被握住的是纸张或数据，而“握住”是一项义务，不是记忆。

senses.title: Fluid that will not leave
senses.definition: the abnormal accumulation of fluid in the body, as in water retention
senses.definitionCN: 体内液体异常积聚，如水肿
senses.example: Swelling in her ankles suggested fluid retention.
senses.exampleCN: 她脚踝肿胀，提示体液潴留。
senses.why: In medicine the body fails to let go of what it should release; the word keeps its physical sense of holding back.
senses.whyCN: 在医学中，身体没能放走本该排出的东西；这个词保留了“拦握不放”的物理义。

senses.title: Soil and materials holding water
senses.titleCN: 保水能力：土壤或材料留住水分
senses.definition: the capacity of a material or soil to hold water or nutrients
senses.definitionCN: 材料或土壤保持水分或养分的能力
senses.example: Clay has high water retention but poor drainage.
senses.exampleCN: 黏土保水性强，但排水差。
senses.why: Agronomy measures retention as a capacity, so the noun becomes a quantity that can be tested.
senses.whyCN: 农学把保持力当作一种可测量的容量，于是这个名词变成一个可检测的量。

senses.title: Money held back
senses.titleCN: 保留金：验收前扣下的一部分款项
senses.definition: a sum withheld from a payment until work is completed or defects are fixed
senses.definitionCN: 在完工或缺陷修复前从付款中扣下的一笔钱
senses.example: The contract withholds five percent as retention for a year.
senses.exampleCN: 合同扣留百分之五作为为期一年的保留金。
senses.why: Construction retains money as leverage; the withheld sum holds the contractor to the promise.
senses.whyCN: 建筑业扣款作为筹码；被扣下的钱把承包商拴在承诺上。

senses.title: Holding heat or flavour
senses.titleCN: 保持：热量、颜色或风味的留存
senses.definition: the ability of something to keep heat, colour, moisture, or flavour
senses.definitionCN: 某物保持热量、颜色、水分或风味的能力
senses.example: The clay pot's heat retention keeps the stew warm for hours.
senses.exampleCN: 砂锅的保温性让炖菜保温数小时。
senses.why: The word applies to any quality that would otherwise escape; a good vessel is one that lets little out.
senses.whyCN: 这个词适用于任何本会逸散的性质；好的容器就是让流失很少的容器。

senses.title: Title kept until payment
senses.titleCN: 所有权保留：货款付清前卖方仍握所有权
senses.definition: a legal arrangement in which a seller keeps ownership of goods until the buyer pays in full
senses.definitionCN: 卖方在买方全额付款前保留货物所有权的法律安排
senses.example: The supplier relied on retention of title when the buyer went bankrupt.
senses.exampleCN: 买方破产时，供应商援引所有权保留条款。
senses.why: Ownership itself is held back as security, so the seller keeps a legal grip on goods already delivered.
senses.whyCN: 所有权本身被扣作担保，卖方因此对已交付的货物保持法律上的抓握。

intro.en: Retention is retain plus -tion. Retain comes from Latin retinere, to hold back, from re-, back, and tenere, to hold.
intro.cn: retention 由 retain 加 -tion 构成。retain 出自拉丁语 retinere“握回、扣住”，由 re-“向后”与 tenere“握持”组成。

items.en: Tenere meant to hold or keep. The root underlies tenant, contain, maintain, and retain.
items.cn: tenere 意为握住、保持。这个词根支撑了 tenant、contain、maintain 与 retain。

items.en: Retinere added re-, back, giving the sense of holding something back or keeping it from escaping.
items.cn: retinere 加上 re-“向后”，得到“拦握某物、不让它跑掉”的意思。

items.en: Retentio named the act of holding back, and in medical writing the retaining of fluid in the body.
items.cn: retentio 指拦握不放的行为，在医学文献中也指体液滞留体内。

items.en: Old French carried the noun into English with both the mental sense of keeping knowledge and the legal sense of keeping possession.
items.cn: 古法语把这个名词带入英语，兼有“把知识留住”的心理义与“保有占有”的法律义。

items.en: The English verb retain covers keeping a fact, a right, a service, or a person, which prepares the broad noun.
items.cn: 英语动词 retain 覆盖保留事实、权利、服务或人员，这为宽泛的名词义铺路。

items.en: Retention later specialized in education as memory retention, in business as staff retention, and in law as retention of title.
items.cn: retention 后来在教育中指记忆保持，在商业中指员工留任，在法律中指所有权保留。

note.en: The first group is the retain family, separated by word class; the second compares words for keeping, memory, and remaining.
note.cn: 第一组是 retain 词族，按词类区分；第二组比较表示保存、记忆与留下的词。

entries.definition: to keep something, or to employ a professional. It names the action.
entries.definitionCN: 保留某物，或聘请专业人士；命名的是动作。

entries.definition: good at remembering or holding things.
entries.definitionCN: 记性好的；有保持力的。

entries.definition: a fee paid to secure a professional's services, or a device that holds teeth in place.
entries.definitionCN: 为确保专业服务而预付的费用，或保持牙齿位置的装置。

entries.definition: keeping something in good condition over time, especially from decay. It stresses protection.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物长期保持良好状态，尤指防止腐坏；强调保护。

entries.definition: the faculty of recalling, or a particular recollection. It names the store rather than the holding.
entries.definitionCN: 回忆的能力，或某段记忆；命名仓储，而非握持。

entries.definition: the work of keeping something in working order. It stresses ongoing effort.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物保持正常运转的工作；强调持续投入。

entries.definition: continuing to exist or act despite difficulty. It stresses duration rather than deliberate keeping.
entries.definitionCN: 遇难仍继续存在或行动；强调持续，而非有意保持。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: re- plus tain plus -tion. The base tenere means to hold, so retention is the holding back of something that might escape.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：re- 加 tain 再加 -tion。词基 tenere 意为握住，所以 retention 是拦住可能跑掉之物。

normal.en: Re plus tain plus tion: hold it back, and keep holding.
normal.cn: re 加 tain 加 tion：拦住它，并且一直握着。

normal.en: Retention of facts is measured by how much leaks out after a week.
normal.cn: 事实的保持，用一周后漏掉多少来衡量。

normal.en: Staff retention counts the people who did not slip away.
normal.cn: 员工留任统计的是没有溜走的人。

normal.en: Clay's water retention means the rain stays where the roots can reach.
normal.cn: 黏土的保水性意味着雨水留在根系能够到的地方。

normal.en: Retention of title keeps the goods legally in the seller's hand until the last payment.
normal.cn: 所有权保留让货物在法律上一直握在卖方手里，直到最后一笔付款。

abstract.en: What a system retains defines what it is; everything else was only passing through.
abstract.cn: 一个系统留下什么，就定义了它是什么；其余都只是路过。

abstract.en: Memory and money obey the same verb: both can be held back.
abstract.cn: 记忆与金钱服从同一个动词：两者都能被扣住不放。

abstract.en: Retention is always selective, and selection is always a judgement about value.
abstract.cn: 留存总是有选择的，而选择总是关于价值的一次判断。

examples.en: The course uses weekly quizzes to test retention rather than speed.
examples.cn: 这门课用每周小测考查保持，而不是速度。

examples.en: Poor retention of new nurses pushed the hospital to redesign shifts.
examples.cn: 新护士留任率低，促使医院重新设计排班。

examples.en: The dam's water retention capacity has fallen by a third after years of silt.
examples.cn: 多年淤积之后，大坝的蓄水能力下降了三成。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（往回）+ ten（握）+ tion——把东西握回来不放，就是保留。

root: 由 retain（保留、保持）加 -tion（名词后缀）构成；retain 出自拉丁语 retinere“握回、扣住”，由 re-“向后”与 tenere“握持”组成，本义为“把可能失去之物拦握不放的行为或能力”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of retention, all circling one idea: something that could leave is held. What is held may be knowledge, employees, records, fluid in the body, water in soil, money withheld, heat in a pot, or legal ownership of goods.
sensesIntro.cn: retention 的八个义项都围绕一个观念：本会离开的东西被握住了。被握住的可以是知识、员工、记录、体内液体、土壤水分、被扣下的款项、锅里的热量，或货物的法律所有权。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a half-closed hand around wet sand, little escaping between the fingers, most staying in the palm.
core.cn: 核心意象：半握的手掌兜住湿沙，指缝漏下的少，掌心留下的多。

chain: RETENTION THE KEEPING OF WHAT MIGHT GO

branches.en: PEOPLE AND KNOWLEDGE: facts kept in memory and staff kept in an organisation.
branches.cn: 人与知识：留在记忆里的事实，留在组织里的员工。

branches.en: FORMAL KEEPING: records held for a required period and money withheld until acceptance.
branches.cn: 形式化的保存：按规定期限留存的记录，以及验收前扣下的款项。

branches.en: PHYSICAL HOLDING: fluid that stays in the body and heat that stays in a pot.
branches.cn: 物理性的握持：滞留在体内的液体，留在锅里的热量。

branches.en: MEASURED CAPACITY: how much water soil or a material can keep.
branches.cn: 可测容量：土壤或材料能保住多少水。

branches.en: LEGAL GRIP: ownership held back as security until payment is complete.
branches.cn: 法律上的抓握：作为担保被扣留的所有权，直到付款完成。

intro.en: Retention is retain plus -tion. The family includes retentive and retainer, with -ive marking the holding quality and -er marking the thing or fee that holds.
intro.cn: retention 由 retain 加 -tion 构成。词族包括 retentive 与 retainer，其中 -ive 标记保持的性质，-er 标记起保持作用之物或费用。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is tenere, extended in retinere and retentio. The same root appears in contain, maintain, and tenant.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基是 tenere，在 retinere 与 retentio 中扩展。同一词根也出现在 contain、maintain 与 tenant 中。

items.example: The root appears in tenant, tenure, and contain.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根出现在 tenant（租户）、tenure（任期）与 contain（包含）中。

items.example: The Latin verb described a fortress retaining its garrison.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词可描述要塞留住驻军。

items.meaning: to keep something or engage a professional

definition_zh: 不溶的；不能溶解的；（问题、矛盾）无法解决的
definition_en: not able to be dissolved in a liquid, or not able to be solved or settled
core_image: 一勺细粉落进水里，沉到底部，搅了很久仍是清清楚楚的一层

（问题、矛盾）无法解决的；不能化解的

senses.title: Will not dissolve in a liquid
senses.definition: not capable of being dissolved in a liquid, so that the substance stays separate and visible
senses.definitionCN: 不能溶解于液体，物质保持分离、看得见
senses.example: The oil remained insoluble in water and floated on top.
senses.exampleCN: 油不溶于水，浮在上面。
senses.why: the negative prefix in- reverses soluble, so the word denies the loosening of particles that soluble describes.
senses.whyCN: 否定前缀 in- 反转 soluble，这个词否认了 soluble 所描述的微粒散开。

senses.title: Insoluble in a named solvent
senses.definition: failing to dissolve in the particular liquid that is named, even though it may dissolve elsewhere
senses.definitionCN: 在被点名的液体中不溶解，尽管在别处可能溶解
senses.example: This pigment is insoluble in alcohol but soluble in acetone.
senses.exampleCN: 这种颜料不溶于酒精，却溶于丙酮。
senses.why: since dissolving is a relation between two substances, a refusal is also a relation and needs the solvent named.
senses.whyCN: 既然溶解是两物之间的关系，拒绝溶解也是一种关系，同样需要点明溶剂。

senses.title: A solid that stays as residue
senses.titleCN: 沉淀下来的不溶固体或残渣
senses.definition: remaining as a solid residue after a liquid has been filtered or poured off
senses.definitionCN: 液体被滤过或倒掉后仍留成固体残渣
senses.example: The insoluble residue was collected on the filter paper.
senses.exampleCN: 不溶残渣被收集在滤纸上。
senses.why: what cannot dissolve must end up somewhere, and in the laboratory it ends up as the residue on the paper.
senses.whyCN: 不能溶解的东西总得有个去处，在实验室里它就成了纸上的残渣。

senses.title: A problem with no apparent answer
senses.definition: unable to be solved or settled, said of a difficulty that resists every proposed remedy
senses.definitionCN: 无法解决或了结，指抵挡一切方案的那种困难
senses.example: The housing shortage seemed insoluble without new land.
senses.exampleCN: 没有新土地，住房短缺似乎无解。
senses.why: the mind unties problems as a liquid unties salts, so a problem that will not come apart is called insoluble.
senses.whyCN: 头脑解问题正如液体解盐，解不开的问题就被叫作 insoluble。

senses.title: A dispute that cannot be reconciled
senses.definition: unable to be brought into agreement, said of opposed claims or interests
senses.definitionCN: 无法使之一致，指对立的主张或利益
senses.example: Their claims were insoluble because both demanded the same field.
senses.exampleCN: 两方都索要同一块地，他们的主张无法调和。
senses.why: two positions that cannot be untied remain locked, which is exactly the image behind the word.
senses.whyCN: 两个解不开的立场会一直互锁，这正是这个词背后的画面。

senses.title: A mystery that cannot be explained
senses.definition: unable to be explained or accounted for, said of a disappearance, a riddle or an event
senses.definitionCN: 无法被解释或说明，指失踪、谜语或某个事件
senses.example: The disappearance remained insoluble for decades.
senses.exampleCN: 那起失踪案数十年没有答案。
senses.why: a riddle is a knot in thought; if no clue loosens it, the knot stays insoluble.
senses.whyCN: 谜语是思路上的结，若没有线索能松开它，这个结就始终解不开。

senses.title: A debt that cannot be discharged
senses.definition: unable to be paid off or discharged, used of an obligation that no arrangement can clear
senses.definitionCN: 无法还清或了结，用于任何安排都清不掉的义务
senses.example: The old debt proved insoluble and was written off.
senses.exampleCN: 那笔旧债无法清偿，最终被注销。
senses.why: a debt is a bond, and to discharge it is to untie it; a bond that cannot be untied is insoluble in the older legal sense.
senses.whyCN: 债务是一种束缚，清偿就是解开；解不开的束缚在旧日法律意义上就是 insoluble。

senses.title: A knot that cannot be untied, an old use
senses.definition: unable to be undone, said of a knot, a band or a fastening in older usage
senses.definitionCN: 旧时用法中指绳结、束带或系缚无法解开
senses.example: The insoluble knot had to be cut with a knife.
senses.exampleCN: 那个死结只能用刀割开。
senses.why: the physical knot is the oldest sense, and every later use keeps the same image of a bond that will not loosen.
senses.whyCN: 实体的绳结是最古老的义项，此后每个用法都保留「束缚不肯松开」这一意象。

intro.en: Insoluble joins the negative prefix in- 'not' to soluble, from Latin insolubilis 'that cannot be loosened or dissolved'. The word is recorded in English from the fourteenth century, with the figurative sense of an unanswerable problem following in the sixteenth. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: insoluble 由否定前缀 in-「不」加 soluble 构成，来自拉丁 insolubilis「不能松开或溶解的」。英语自十四世纪有记录，十六世纪出现「问题无解」的比喻义。年代均为约数。

items.en: Solvere 'to loosen, untie, dissolve' is built from se- 'apart' and luere 'to loosen'; the same verb yields solve, solution and dissolve.
items.cn: solvere「松开、解开、溶解」由 se-「分开」与 luere「松开」构成，同一动词衍生 solve、solution 与 dissolve。

items.en: In- 'not' plus solubilis 'able to be dissolved' produced insolubilis, used of knots that would not come undone as well as of substances that would not dissolve.
items.cn: in-「不」加 solubilis「可被溶解的」构成 insolubilis，既用于解不开的绳结，也用于不能溶解的物质。

items.en: Old French insoluble brought the word into English in the fourteenth century, at first almost entirely in the physical sense.
items.cn: 古法语 insoluble 在十四世纪把这个词带入英语，最初几乎全是实体义。

items.en: Seventeenth-century chemistry made the word a standard label for solids that a solvent leaves untouched, and the laboratory phrase insoluble residue dates from this period.
items.cn: 十七世纪的化学把这个词变成溶剂动不了的固体的标准标签，实验室里把这类残渣称为「不溶残渣」，这一说法即出自这一时期。

items.en: By the sixteenth century insoluble was applied to problems and disputes that no remedy could settle, borrowing the chemical image for the mind.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，insoluble 被用于任何办法都了结不了的问题与争端，把化学意象借给了头脑。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin and first citation): the pre-Latin form of luere is a reconstruction, and no exact date is recorded for the first English use of the figurative sense.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与首见书证）：luere 在拉丁语之前的形式属于重构，比喻义在英语中最早使用的确切年代没有记录。

note.en: Group one holds the negative forms that look interchangeable but answer different questions; group two holds words for things that resist solution or passage.
note.cn: 第一组是看起来可互换、实际回答不同问题的否定形式；第二组是表示抗拒溶解或通过之物的词。

entries.definition: The exact opposite in the chemical sense; it also carries the sense of a solvable problem, which insoluble mirrors.
entries.definitionCN: 化学义上完全相反；它也带「问题可解」义，insoluble 与之对应。

entries.definition: A plain English negative used only for problems and puzzles, with no chemical sense at all.
entries.definitionCN: 纯英语否定形式，只用于问题与谜题，完全没有化学义。

entries.definition: A separate adjective meaning 'not solvable', built on solvable rather than on soluble; it never describes a substance.
entries.definitionCN: 另一个形容词，意为「不可解」，由 solvable 而非 soluble 构成；从不形容物质。

entries.definition: Built on dissolve: it describes ties, vows or unions that cannot be broken, not salts that will not dissolve.
entries.definitionCN: 由 dissolve 构成：描述无法解除的联系、誓言或结合，而非不溶解的盐。

entries.definition: Describes a problem or person that is hard to manage, but not necessarily impossible; insoluble is stronger.
entries.definitionCN: 形容难以处理的问题或人，但未必不可能；insoluble 语气更强。

entries.definition: Describes a barrier that fluid cannot pass through; it is about passage, not about dissolving.
entries.definitionCN: 形容流体无法穿过的屏障；说的是通过，不是溶解。

entries.definition: Used of conflicts or doubts that cannot be resolved, close to the dispute sense of insoluble.
entries.definitionCN: 用于无法化解的冲突或疑虑，接近 insoluble 的争端义。

entries.definition: An everyday adjective for something that will not give way, used of people, stains and problems alike.
entries.definitionCN: 日常形容词，指不肯让步之物，可用于人、污渍与问题。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: In- 'not' on top of soluble: the loosening is denied.

normal.en: The pair runs soluble and insoluble, solubility and insolubility.

normal.en: Everyday phrases mark the figurative sense: an insoluble problem, an insoluble conflict.

normal.en: Do not confuse it with insolvable, which is built on solvable and applies only to questions.

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one refusal to loosen: powder stays on the bottom, a named solvent gets no answer, residue remains on the paper, a problem and a dispute will not untie, a mystery keeps its secret, a debt cannot be discharged, and finally an old knot has to be cut.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一次「拒绝松开」：粉末留在杯底，指定溶剂得不到回应，残渣留在滤纸上，问题与争端解不开，谜团守着秘密，债务清不掉，最后是一个旧绳结只能用刀割断。

branches.en: REFUSED DISSOLVING: the bare denial and the solvent-specific denial are one refusal seen twice.
branches.cn: 拒绝溶解：笼统的否定与对指定溶剂的否定，是同一次拒绝的两种看法。

branches.en: RESIDUE: what will not dissolve has to remain somewhere, and the laboratory makes that place visible.
branches.cn: 残渣：不溶之物总得留在某处，实验室让这个去处看得见。

branches.en: LOCKED IN THE MIND: a problem and a dispute are knots no remedy can loosen.

branches.en: UNEXPLAINED AND UNPAID: a mystery keeps its secret and a debt keeps its bond.

branches.en: THE OLDEST KNOT: the physical knot that must be cut is the root image of every later sense.

scene: 楼下有人开始练鼓，整栋楼都被那阵喧闹震得发慌。 Someone started practising drums downstairs and the whole building shook with the racket.
sceneCN: 这里 racket 指喧闹声（第 1 个义项：吵闹的声响）；句意为楼下有人开始练鼓，整栋楼都被那阵喧闹震得发慌。

pos.zh: 球拍；喧闹声；非法生意
吵闹；喧哗

senses.title: A tennis racket
senses.definition: a bat with a netted face used in ball games
senses.definitionCN: 球类运动中带网面的拍子
senses.example: She kept her racket in the car so she could play after work.
senses.exampleCN: 她把球拍放在车里，下班后就能去打。
senses.why: The concrete sense is the oldest and the most physical.
senses.whyCN: 具体义项最古老，也最物理。

senses.title: The racket of traffic
senses.definition: a loud, confused noise that goes on and on
senses.definitionCN: 持续不断、混杂的响亮声响
senses.example: Someone started practising drums downstairs and the whole building shook with the racket.
senses.exampleCN: 楼下有人开始练鼓，整栋楼都被那阵喧闹震得发慌。
senses.why: The word judges the noise as excessive, not merely loud.
senses.whyCN: 这个词判定这声响过分，而不只是响。

senses.title: A protection racket
senses.definition: an illegal business that sells safety it also threatens
senses.definitionCN: 既威胁安全又出售安全的非法生意
senses.example: The shop owners paid a protection racket for years.
senses.exampleCN: 店主们多年来向一个收取保护费的团伙交钱。
senses.why: The criminal sense grew from the idea of a noisy disturbance.
senses.whyCN: 犯罪义项从「吵闹骚扰」的意思长出来。

senses.title: A racket of complaints
senses.definition: a chorus of protest from many voices at once
senses.definitionCN: 许多声音同时发出的抗议
senses.example: The new timetable raised a racket of complaints from parents.
senses.exampleCN: 新时间表引来了家长们一片抱怨声。
senses.why: The word can describe a human chorus, not only machines.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以描述人声的合唱，不只是机器。

senses.title: To racket about
senses.definition: to move around making noise and disturbance
senses.definitionCN: 四处走动、发出噪音与骚扰
senses.example: The children racketed through the house until dusk.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们在屋里闹到天黑。
senses.why: The verb keeps the noise as an activity.
senses.whyCN: 动词把噪音当作一种活动。

senses.title: A numbers racket
senses.definition: an illegal lottery or betting operation
senses.definitionCN: 非法的彩票或赌博经营
senses.example: The numbers racket ran out of a barbershop.
senses.exampleCN: 那个地下彩票勾当就在一家理发店里运作。
senses.why: This is the organised-crime sense in its classic form.
senses.whyCN: 这是有组织犯罪义项的经典形态。

senses.title: A rackety old car
senses.definition: a machine that is noisy and in poor condition
senses.definitionCN: 吵闹且状况不佳的机器
senses.example: They toured the coast in a rackety old car.
senses.exampleCN: 他们开着一辆破旧吵闹的老车沿海岸旅行。
senses.why: The adjective extends the noise to the object itself.
senses.whyCN: 形容词把噪音延伸到了物件本身。

senses.title: Versus noise
senses.definition: a din that is judged excessive and annoying, as opposed to any sound
senses.definitionCN: 被判定为过分而恼人的喧闹，与任何声音相对
senses.example: Noise can be measured; a racket is complained about.
senses.exampleCN: noise 可以被测量，racket 会被投诉。
senses.why: The pair separates a physical event from a social judgement.
senses.whyCN: 这一对词把物理事件与社会评判分开。

intro.en: Racket has two histories: the bat probably comes from French raquette, while the noise may be imitative.
intro.cn: racket 有两条历史：球拍大概来自法语 raquette，喧闹义则可能是拟声的。

items.en: The bat came through French from an Arabic root.
items.cn: 球拍经法语来自一个阿拉伯词根。

items.en: The din sense probably echoes the sound itself.
items.cn: 喧闹义很可能是对声音本身的模仿。

items.en: London slang turned a disturbance into an extortion scheme.
items.cn: 伦敦俚语把骚扰变成敲诈勾当。

items.en: Lawn tennis fixed the bat as the main sense.
items.cn: 草地网球把球拍固定为主要义项。

items.en: Today the word covers sport, noise and crime at once.
items.cn: 今天这个词同时覆盖运动、噪音与犯罪。

note.en: The look-alike group is the rack- family; the near-meaning group separates din, clamour, commotion and racketeering.
note.cn: 形近组是 rack 词族；近义组把「喧闹」「嘈杂」「骚动」「敲诈」分开。

entries.definition: an alternative spelling of the bat.
entries.definitionCN: 球拍的另一种拼法。

entries.definition: a vehicle driven by thrust.
entries.definitionCN: 靠推力飞行的飞行器。

entries.definition: a frame for storing things.
entries.definitionCN: 存放物品的架子。

entries.definition: noisy and badly worn.
entries.definitionCN: 喧闹且破旧的。

entries.definition: a loud unpleasant noise.
entries.definitionCN: 响亮难听的声音。

entries.definition: loud confused shouting.
entries.definitionCN: 响亮混乱的喊叫。

entries.definition: noisy disturbance.
entries.definitionCN: 喧闹的骚动。

entries.definition: running an illegal business.
entries.definitionCN: 经营非法生意。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep both pictures: a bat on a table and a noise coming through the floor.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想同时留住两幅画面：桌上的球拍，和从地板传来的响声。

normal.en: Racket covers bat and noise: one object, one disturbance.
normal.cn: racket 兼指球拍与噪音：一件东西，一种骚扰。

normal.en: Picture a tennis racket on a table while drums shake the floor.
normal.cn: 想象桌上放着一只网球拍，鼓声震着地板。

normal.en: Say RAK-it; it sounds short and hard, like a slap.
normal.cn: 读 RAK-it，听起来短而硬，像一记拍打。

normal.en: The criminal sense came from the noise of harassment.
normal.cn: 犯罪义项来自骚扰的噪音。

normal.en: Ask which racket is meant: sport, sound or scheme?
normal.cn: 问清是哪种 racket：运动、声音，还是勾当？

abstract.en: A racket is noise with a purpose when someone is being shaken down.
abstract.cn: 当有人被敲诈时，喧闹就带上了目的。

abstract.en: The word joins the tool and the disturbance: both are things you swing.
abstract.cn: 这个词把工具与骚扰连在一起：两者都是可以挥动的东西。

abstract.en: Every racket needs an audience, whether a crowd or a victim.
abstract.cn: 每个 racket 都需要观众，无论是一群人还是一名受害者。

root: 法语 raquette（球拍）；喧闹义可能为拟声

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses swing between object and noise: a bat, a din, a criminal scheme, a chorus, the act of making noise, a lottery, a broken car and the contrast with plain noise.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项在物件与声响之间摆动：球拍、喧闹、犯罪勾当、一片人声、吵闹的动作、地下彩票、破车，以及与单纯噪音的对照。

latinIntro.cn: 法语 raquette 提供球拍义，可能来自阿拉伯语 rakdat（手掌）；喧闹义没有确定的词根。

definition_zh: vt. 赞同；支持；（在票据背面）签名背书；把费用记入
definition_en: to say publicly that you support or approve of someone or something, or to sign the back of a cheque so that it passes to another person
core_image: 一张支票被翻过来，签名落在背面的空白处；另一位政治人物的名字被印在候选人海报的下方
scene: 竞选集会上，前任部长举起草率支持信。 The former minister chose to endorse the younger candidate.
sceneCN: 这里 endorse 指「公开支持」（第 1 个义项：公开表态赞同或支持某人）；句意是那位前任部长选择支持更年轻的候选人。

pos.zh: 赞同；支持；背书；在背面签名

senses.title: To back someone publicly
senses.definition: to announce publicly that you support a person, policy or product
senses.definitionCN: （动词）公开宣布支持某人、某政策或某产品
senses.example: The former minister chose to endorse the younger candidate.
senses.exampleCN: 那位前任部长选择支持更年轻的候选人。
senses.why: A famous name printed in large letters under a candidate poster
senses.whyCN: 候选人海报下方用大字印着一位名人名字

senses.title: To approve officially
senses.definition: to give official approval to a report or proposal
senses.definitionCN: （动词）对报告或提案给予正式批准
senses.example: The committee endorsed the report without changing it.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会未作修改便认可了这份报告。
senses.why: A rubber stamp coming down on the last page of a report
senses.whyCN: 报告最后一页上盖下的橡皮图章

senses.title: To sign the back
senses.definition: to sign the back of a cheque or note so that it passes to someone else
senses.definitionCN: （动词）在支票或票据背面签名，使它转归他人
senses.example: She endorsed the cheque and handed it over the desk.
senses.exampleCN: 她在支票背面签了字，把它递过桌面。
senses.why: A pen turning a cheque over to write on its blank back
senses.whyCN: 一支笔把支票翻过来，在空白的背面写字

senses.title: To charge to an account
senses.definition: to add an extra cost to what a customer has to pay
senses.definitionCN: （动词）把额外费用加到客户应付的款项上
senses.example: The bank endorsed the fee to his current account.
senses.exampleCN: 银行把这笔费用记入他的活期账户。
senses.why: A small line added at the foot of a bill
senses.whyCN: 账单末尾添上的一行小字

intro.en: Endorse is en- plus Latin dorsum, the back; to endorse is literally to write on the back of a document, and the sense of public approval grew out of that signature on the reverse.
intro.cn: endorse 由 en- 加拉丁语 dorsum（背）构成，字面义就是在文件背面写字；公开支持这一含义正是从背面的那行签名引申而来。

items.en: Dorsum is the Latin word for the back.
items.cn: dorsum 是拉丁语中的背部一词。

items.en: Old French dos, back, comes down from dorsum.
items.cn: 古法语 dos 意为背部，由 dorsum 而来。

items.en: Dorsare means to write on the back of a document.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 dorsare 意为在文件背面书写。

items.en: Endorse enters English for signing on the reverse.
items.cn: 16 世纪 endorse 进入英语，指在背面签名。

items.en: The older spelling indorse stays in law and banking.
items.cn: 旧拼写 indorse 保留在法律与银行业务中。

items.en: To endorse becomes standard language for backing a candidate.
items.cn: endorse 成为支持候选人的标准竞选用语。

note.en: Endorse, dorsal and dossier all go back to Latin dorsum, the back; endorsement is the noun of the act, and indorse is the older spelling still met on cheques.
note.cn: endorse、dorsal 与 dossier 都可追到拉丁语 dorsum（背）；endorsement 是该行为的名词，indorse 是票据上仍能见到的旧拼法。

examples.en: The party endorsed the report after a long debate.
examples.cn: 经过长时间讨论，该党认可了这份报告。

dict_mnemonic.text: endorse ＝ en-（使…）＋ dors（背，拉丁 dorsum）＋ -e ＝「写在背面」。先在背面签名，再由签名推出「支持、认可」。名词 endorsement 支持与背书，受款人 endorsee 是被背书的一方。三个用法：公开支持 endorse a candidate、正式认可 formally endorse a report、票据背书 endorse a cheque。旧拼法 indorse 仍常见于法律与银行文本。同根还有 dorsal 背部的、dossier 案卷，都出自 dorsum。

root: 拉丁语 dorsum（背部）→ 古法语 dos（背）→ endorse（在背面签名；支持）

sensesIntro.en: Four uses: public support, official approval, a signature on the back, and a cost charged to an account
sensesIntro.cn: 四种用法：公开支持、正式认可、背面签名，以及把费用记入账户

definition_zh: 隐秘贮藏处；贮藏物；（计算机）高速缓存；隐藏贮存
definition_en: a hidden store of goods or data; as a verb, to store or hide away
core_image: 树根下埋着的一只铁皮箱，装着猎人的补给
scene: 猎人在老松树的根下挖出一只锈迹斑斑的铁箱。 The trapper kept a cache of supplies by the river.
sceneCN: 这里 cache 是「隐秘贮藏物」（第 1 个义项：暗中存放的补给）；句意是猎人在河边藏了一批补给品。

pos.zh: 隐藏的贮藏物；秘密贮藏处；（计算机）高速缓存
隐藏；贮藏；（计算机）缓存

derivatives.zh: 由法语 diminutive 而来，义为「小型藏匿处」
由 geo- 加 cache 构成的复合词，义为「地理藏宝点」
同源近形词，义为「现金」，与 cache 发音相同

senses.title: A hidden store of goods
senses.definition: a secret store of supplies or valuables hidden away for later use
senses.definitionCN: 为日后取用而秘密藏起的物资或财物
senses.example: Soldiers found a cache of rifles in the barn.
senses.exampleCN: 士兵在谷仓里发现一批私藏的步枪。
senses.why: The French word for a hiding place named the things hidden there.
senses.whyCN: 法语的「藏匿处」一词转指藏起来的东西。

senses.title: A fast computer memory
senses.definition: a small, fast memory that keeps copies of frequently used data
senses.definitionCN: 保存常用数据副本的小型高速存储器
senses.example: Clearing the browser cache fixed the slow loading.
senses.exampleCN: 清掉浏览器缓存后，加载变快了。
senses.why: Computing borrowed the image of a small store kept close at hand.
senses.whyCN: 计算机术语借用了「近旁小库」这一意象。

senses.title: To store or hide away
senses.definition: to put something in a hidden store, literally or in computing
senses.definitionCN: 把某物藏入密藏处，计算领域指存入缓存
senses.example: The rebels cached their ammunition in caves.
senses.exampleCN: 叛军把弹药藏进山洞。
senses.why: The noun of the store becomes the verb of storing.
senses.whyCN: 贮藏物的名词转为贮藏的动词。

intro.en: Cache comes from French cacher, to hide, whose deeper root is the Latin coacticare, to press together.
intro.cn: cache 源自法语 cacher（隐藏），更深的词根是拉丁语 coacticare（压紧收拢）。

items.en: coacticare meant to press or force together, from coactus, compelled.
items.cn: 拉丁语 coacticare 意为「压紧、收拢」，出自 coactus（被迫的）。

items.en: cachier and cacher meant to press, then to hide away.
items.cn: 古法语 cachier、cacher 由「压紧」转指「藏匿」。

items.en: cache named a hiding place, especially for furs and supplies.
items.cn: 法语名词 cache 指藏匿处，尤指皮货与补给的存放点。

items.en: fur traders and explorers brought cache into English for hidden stores.
items.cn: 十八至十九世纪皮货商与探险家把 cache 带入英语，指密藏的物资。

items.en: computer engineers adopted cache for a small fast store of data.

definition_zh: 云的形成；云的形态；成云过程
definition_en: the process in which moist air cools and its vapour turns into a visible cloud, or a cloud mass so formed
core_image: 山谷里升起的水汽在半山腰遇冷，聚成一团看得见的白絮
scene: 清晨山谷中水汽沿坡上升，在半山腰聚成一团白絮。 Orographic lift produced a cloud formation along the ridge by mid-morning.
sceneCN: 这里指「水汽受地形抬升、冷却凝结而成云的过程」（第 1 个义项：湿空气上升冷却、水汽变成可见云体的过程）；句意为地形抬升在上午过半时沿山脊生成了一片云。图中可辨识物件：山坡、上升的水汽、白絮状云团、山脊线。

pos.zh: 云的形成；云体形态

senses.title: The process by which a cloud comes into being
senses.titleCN: 水汽冷却凝结而成云的过程
senses.definition: the process in which rising moist air cools and its water vapour condenses into a visible cloud
senses.definitionCN: 上升的湿空气冷却、其中的水汽凝结成可见云体的过程
senses.example: Orographic lift produced a cloud formation along the ridge by mid-morning.
senses.exampleCN: 地形抬升在上午过半时沿山脊生成了一片云。
senses.why: Cloud is an Old English word for a mass of rock or hill, later transferred to a mass in the sky; formation comes from Latin forma 'shape' plus -atio, so the phrase names both the shaping and the thing shaped.
senses.whyCN: cloud 是古英语中表示「岩块、山丘」的词，后来移指天上的团块；formation 来自拉丁 forma「形状」加 -atio，因此这个短语同时指「成形」与「成形之物」。

senses.title: A visible cloud mass of a particular shape
senses.titleCN: 具有特定形状的可见云体
senses.definition: a body of cloud with a recognisable outline as seen from the ground
senses.definitionCN: 从地面看去轮廓可辨的一团云
senses.example: A striking cloud formation hung over the valley at dusk.
senses.exampleCN: 黄昏时一片引人注目的云悬在山谷上方。
senses.why: The noun formation can name the result as well as the act, so a cloud formation is simply a formation made of cloud.
senses.whyCN: 名词 formation 既可指动作也可指结果，因此 cloud formation 就是「由云构成的成形之物」。

senses.title: The condensation step onto tiny nuclei
senses.titleCN: 水汽在凝结核上凝结的环节
senses.definition: the microphysical step in which vapour condenses on dust, salt or ice nuclei
senses.definitionCN: 水汽在尘埃、盐粒或冰核等凝结核上凝结的微观环节
senses.example: Dust from the dry lakebed sped up cloud formation downwind.
senses.exampleCN: 干涸湖床扬起的尘埃加快了下风方向的成云。
senses.why: Formation here narrows to one stage of the process, because droplets need a surface before they can appear.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 formation 收窄为过程中的一个环节，因为液滴必须先有依附的表面才能出现。

senses.title: An organised cloud pattern seen from above
senses.titleCN: 从空中看到的成片云系格局
senses.definition: an organised pattern of cloud tops visible in satellite imagery
senses.definitionCN: 卫星图像中可见的、有组织的云顶分布格局
senses.example: The satellite tracked cloud formation over the basin each hour.
senses.exampleCN: 卫星每小时追踪该盆地上空的成云格局。
senses.why: Seen from orbit the emphasis shifts from one cloud to the arrangement, and formation takes its sense of an ordered pattern.
senses.whyCN: 从轨道上看，重点从一朵云转到云的排列，formation 于是取「有秩序的格局」之义。

senses.title: A recognised cloud type in a classification
senses.titleCN: 云分类体系中的一个云型
senses.definition: one of the named genera or species of cloud used in meteorological classification
senses.definitionCN: 气象分类中命名的云属或云种之一
senses.example: The observer logged the cloud formation as altocumulus lenticularis.
senses.exampleCN: 观测员把这片云记为荚状高积云。
senses.why: Meteorology borrowed the phrase for the units of its classification, since each type is a stable, repeatable shape.
senses.whyCN: 气象学借用这个短语来指分类的单位，因为每一类都是一种稳定、可重复的形状。

senses.title: Cloud created by human action
senses.definition: cloud produced deliberately by seeding or unintentionally by an industrial plume
senses.definitionCN: 通过播撒作业有意生成、或由工业烟羽无意生成的云
senses.example: Seeding the deck led to cloud formation within twenty minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 对云层播撒后二十分钟内便出现了成云。
senses.why: The phrase needed no new word for artificial clouds; formation simply took an agent, human or otherwise.
senses.whyCN: 人造云不需要新词，formation 只要带上施动者即可，无论这施动者是人还是别的因素。

senses.title: A dense mass of things resembling cloud
senses.titleCN: 比喻：形似云团的密集聚集物
senses.definition: a dense gathering of dust, insects or particles that looks like a cloud
senses.definitionCN: 尘埃、昆虫或微粒密集聚拢、形似云团的状态
senses.example: A cloud formation of midges rose from the marsh at sunset.
senses.exampleCN: 日落时沼泽上方升起一片形似云团的蠓虫。
senses.why: Because cloud had long meant any drifting mass, the phrase extends naturally to anything that hangs and moves like one.
senses.whyCN: cloud 早已泛指任何飘浮的团块，因此这个短语自然延伸到一切像云那样悬浮移动的东西。

senses.title: The stage at which an idea takes shape
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：想法开始成形的阶段
senses.definition: the point at which an idea or plan begins to take a visible, workable shape
senses.definitionCN: 想法或计划开始呈现出可见、可操作的形态的阶段
senses.example: The proposal was still in cloud formation when the budget froze.
senses.exampleCN: 预算冻结时，这个提案还处在刚刚成形的阶段。
senses.why: The metaphor keeps the physical steps: something scattered gathers, cools and becomes one visible body.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留了物理步骤：散乱之物聚拢、冷却，最后成为一个可见的整体。

intro.en: Cloud formation joins an Old English word for a mass of rock with a Latin-derived noun of shaping. The compound itself is modern and transparent. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: cloud formation 由一个古英语的「岩块」词与一个拉丁来源的「成形」名词合成。这个复合词本身是近代的，构词透明。年代均为约数。

items.en: Clud meant 'a mass of rock, a hill'. The sense 'visible mass in the sky' is recorded from the thirteenth century, probably through the image of a heap floating overhead.
items.cn: clūd 意为「岩块、山丘」。指「天上的可见团块」的义项自十三世纪有记录，可能来自「悬浮的堆积物」这一意象。

items.en: Forma meant 'shape, mould, outline'. Its deeper origin is not established; the link sometimes proposed to Greek morphē is a hypothesis rather than a proven cognate.
items.cn: forma 意为「形状、模子、轮廓」。其更深来源未得到证明；有人提出的与希腊 morphē 的联系只是假说，并非已证实的同源关系。

items.en: Formare 'to shape' plus -atio produced formatio 'a shaping, a forming', the direct source of English formation.
items.cn: formare「使成形」加 -atio 构成 formatio「成形、塑造」，是英语 formation 的直接来源。

items.en: Cloud and formation were combined in English scientific writing to name the making of a cloud; the phrase is a native construction, not a Latin loan.
items.cn: cloud 与 formation 在英语科技写作中组合起来，用来指云的形成；这个短语是英语自身的构造，并非拉丁语借词。

items.en: From the nineteenth century the phrase was fixed in meteorology both for the process and for a classified cloud shape.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，这个短语在气象学中固定下来，既指过程，也指分类上的云形。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin only): the pre-Old-English origin of clud is unsettled and is related to clod; any Indo-European form offered for it is a reconstruction. The first date of the compound is only approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅更深词源）：clūd 在古英语之前的来源无定论，与 clod 有亲缘；凡为其提出的印欧形式均属重构。该复合词的首见年代只能约计。

note.en: Group one holds other cloud compounds that share the element cloud but name different things; group two holds words for cloud, cloudiness and the underlying condensation.
note.cn: 第一组是同样含 cloud 一词、但所指不同的复合词；第二组是表示云、云量以及底层凝结过程的词。

entries.definition: The share of the sky obscured by cloud, a measured quantity rather than a process of forming.
entries.definitionCN: 天空被云遮蔽的比例，是一个可测量的量，而非成云的过程。

entries.definition: The practice of adding particles to a cloud to make it rain; it acts on an existing cloud instead of naming its formation.
entries.definitionCN: 向云中播撒微粒以促降水的作业；它作用于已有的云，而不指云的形成。

entries.definition: A brief, violent downpour; it names the precipitation that follows, not the cloud that produced it.
entries.definitionCN: 短促猛烈的暴雨；它指随之而来的降水，而非造出降水的云。

entries.definition: The visible mass of droplets in the sky; cloud formation names how that mass comes about.
entries.definitionCN: 空中可见的液滴团块；cloud formation 指这团块如何生成。

entries.definition: The condition of being cloudy, a state measured over time, while formation is an event with stages.
entries.definitionCN: 多云的状态，是随时间测量的状态，而成形是有阶段的事件。

entries.definition: The change from vapour to liquid, one step within cloud formation rather than the whole process.
entries.definitionCN: 由气态变为液态，是成云过程中的一步，而非整个过程。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Cloud was first a heap of rock; a heap in the sky kept the same name.
normal.cn: cloud 最初指一堆岩石；天上的堆状物沿用了同一个名字。

normal.en: Formation is forma 'shape' plus -atio, so the phrase is literally 'cloud shaping'.
normal.cn: formation 是 forma「形状」加 -atio，因此这个短语字面就是「云的成形」。

normal.en: The family runs form, formation, formative, reform, conform and formless.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 form、formation、formative、reform、conform 与 formless。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the process sense: cloud formation process, rapid cloud formation, cloud formation and precipitation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出过程义：成云过程、快速成云、成云与降水。

normal.en: Meteorology uses the phrase for a classified shape, as in altocumulus lenticularis.
normal.cn: 气象学用这个短语指分类上的云形，如荚状高积云。

abstract.en: Picture a kettle's steam gathering into one white shape under a cold window.
abstract.cn: 想象水壶的蒸汽在冷窗前聚成一个白色的形状。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd drifting together until it has a visible outline.
abstract.cn: 想象人群慢慢聚拢，直到有了看得见的轮廓。

abstract.en: Picture a rough idea cooling into a shape you could hand to someone.
abstract.cn: 想象一个粗糙的想法冷却定型，成了可以交给别人的东西。

examples.en: The satellite tracked cloud formation over the basin each hour.
examples.cn: 卫星每小时追踪该盆地上空的成云。

examples.en: Warm ocean air drives cloud formation along the coast.
examples.cn: 温暖的海洋空气推动沿岸成云。

examples.en: A striking cloud formation hung over the valley at dusk.
examples.cn: 黄昏时一片引人注目的云悬在山谷上方。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「cloud（云）+ formation（形成）」——水汽在天上排队成形 → 云的形成

root: 英语复合词：cloud 来自古英语 clūd「岩块、山丘」，后移指天上的云团，更深来源不确定；formation 来自拉丁 forma「形状」加 -atio。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one event: scattered vapour gathers, cools, becomes a visible body, is classified, is seen from above, is made on purpose, and finally lends its shape to dust clouds and to ideas.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个事件展开：散乱的水汽聚拢、冷却、成为可见的团块，被分类、被从空中看到、被人为制造，最后把「成形」这一形状借给尘埃团与想法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: vapour rising along a slope cools and gathers into one white mass.
core.cn: 核心意象：水汽沿坡上升、遇冷，聚成一团白絮。

branches.en: MAKING: the process and its microphysical step both describe vapour becoming droplets.
branches.cn: 生成：过程与其中的微观环节都描述水汽变成液滴。

branches.en: SHAPE SEEN: from the ground or from orbit, the point is an outline one can recognise.
branches.cn: 所见之形：无论从地面还是从轨道，要点都是可辨认的轮廓。

branches.en: CLASSIFICATION: a repeatable shape becomes a named type.
branches.cn: 分类：可重复的形状成为一个有名字的类型。

branches.en: MADE ON PURPOSE: seeding works on the same steps with an added agent.
branches.cn: 人为制造：播撒作业在同一批步骤上加入施动者。

branches.en: TRANSFERRED SHAPE: dust clouds and ideas borrow the gathering outline.
branches.cn: 形状转移：尘埃团与想法借用了这种聚拢的轮廓。

intro.en: The phrase is a native English compound whose second element is a Latin derivative, so it can be read both as English words and as morphemes.
intro.cn: 这个短语是英语自身的复合词，第二个成分是拉丁来源的派生词，因此既可以按英语词读，也可以按语素读。

latinIntro.en: Latin forma gives form, formation, formative and formless; the prefix in reform and conform comes from re- 'again' and con- 'together'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 forma 衍生 form、formation、formative 与 formless；reform 与 conform 的前缀分别来自 re-「再」与 con-「共同」。

senses.definitionCN: 把成本、数量或时间加入计算
senses.example: Good planners take into account the cost of repair, not only the price of purchase.
senses.exampleCN: 好的规划者会把修理成本计入，而不只看购买价格。
senses.why: Here the factor has a number, so the image of the ledger becomes literal.
senses.whyCN: 这里因素带有数字，账本意象变成字面用法。

senses.title: Considering someone's feelings
senses.definition: to allow for other people's needs or feelings
senses.definitionCN: 把别人的需求或感受纳入考虑
senses.example: Good hosts take into account the dietary needs of every guest.
senses.exampleCN: 周到的主人会顾及每位客人的饮食需求。
senses.why: The account book turns social: what is entered is another person's comfort.
senses.whyCN: 账本转向社交：记入的是他人的舒适。

senses.title: Weighing a risk
senses.definition: to include a possible hazard when assessing a plan
senses.definitionCN: 评估计划时把可能的危险纳入
senses.example: Engineers must take into account the risk of flooding.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师必须把洪水风险考虑在内。
senses.why: A hazard is entered as a line in the assessment, so it changes the final tally.
senses.whyCN: 危险作为一条评估项目被记入，因此会改变最终合计。

senses.title: Balancing pros and cons
senses.definition: to weigh advantages against disadvantages before deciding
senses.definitionCN: 决定前把利与弊放在一起衡量
senses.example: Committees take into account both the benefits and the disruption.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会会兼顾收益与扰动。
senses.why: Both columns are entered on the same page, so neither can be ignored.
senses.whyCN: 两栏都记在同一页上，任何一栏都无法被忽略。

senses.title: Reserving time or cost in planning
senses.titleCN: 规划时预留时间或成本
senses.definition: to allow time or money for something in a schedule or budget
senses.definitionCN: 在日程或预算中为某事留出时间或钱
senses.example: Builders take into account the weeks lost to rain.
senses.exampleCN: 施工方会把因雨损失的那几周计算在内。
senses.why: Time and money are quantities, and an unentered quantity is never budgeted.
senses.whyCN: 时间与金钱都是数量，未记入的数量就从未被预算。

senses.title: Failing to allow for something
senses.definition: used in the negative to say that something was overlooked
senses.definitionCN: 用否定式说明某因素被忽略
senses.example: These models do not take into account the cost of transport.
senses.exampleCN: 这些模型没有把运输成本考虑在内。
senses.why: The negative form is the usual way to criticise a model or a plan.
senses.whyCN: 否定式是批评模型或计划的常用方式。

senses.title: Before making a decision
senses.definition: used to describe the stage before a choice is fixed
senses.definitionCN: 选择定下之前的阶段
senses.example: The board will take into account the latest survey before voting.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会在投票前会把最新调查考虑进去。
senses.why: The entry is made before the vote, so the phrase marks sequence rather than content.
senses.whyCN: 记入发生在投票之前，因此短语标记的是顺序而非内容。

senses.title: As one variable in a model
senses.titleCN: 作为模型中的一个变量
senses.definition: used in statistics to say that a variable enters a model
senses.definitionCN: 在统计中说明某变量进入模型
senses.example: The model can take into account age as well as income.
senses.exampleCN: 该模型可以把年龄与收入一并纳入。
senses.why: A model is a ledger of variables, and only what is entered can affect the output.
senses.whyCN: 模型是变量的账本，只有记入的才能影响输出。

intro.en: Take comes from Old Norse taka, to grasp, which replaced the older English verb in the medieval period. Account comes through Old French acont from Latin computare, to reckon, built on com-, together, and putare, to think or reckon; the deeper origin of putare has more than one explanation. The phrase is modern and its first date is approximate.
intro.cn: take 来自古诺斯语 taka「抓取」，在中古英语时期取代了更早的本族动词。account 经古法语 acont 来自拉丁语 computare「计算」，由 com-「一起」与 putare「思量、计算」构成；putare 的更深来源有不止一种解释。短语属近代，首见年代为约数。

items.en: Taka meant to grasp or seize and gradually replaced the native verb.
items.cn: taka 意为「抓取」，逐渐取代了本族动词。

items.en: Computare means to reckon together, the source of count and compute.
items.cn: computare 意为「合起来计算」，是 count 与 compute 的来源。

items.en: Putare meant to think or reckon; a proposed link to pruning is not settled.
items.cn: putare 意为「思量、计算」；把它与「修剪」相联的说法尚无定论。

items.en: Old French acont named a reckoning or a settled bill.
items.cn: 古法语 acont 指一次结算或已结清的账单。

items.en: English account keeps both the ledger sense and the sense of explanation.
items.cn: 英语的 account 兼有账目与说明两义。

items.en: The frame is modern; first dates are approximate.
items.cn: 这一框架属近代用法，首见年代为约数。

note.en: The first group shares the same image but changes one word; the second group holds verbs of consideration.
note.cn: 第一组共用同一意象而更换一个词；第二组是表示考量的动词。

entries.definition: The shorter form drops into and is slightly more formal.
entries.definitionCN: 较短形式省去一个介词，略正式一些。

entries.definition: It is a near synonym and often interchangeable.
entries.definitionCN: 它几乎是同义词，常可互换。

entries.definition: It means to assume something without allowing for it, the reverse of this phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 意为想当然而不予考虑，与本短语相反。

entries.definition: The same verb with another particle means to assume control.
entries.definitionCN: 同一动词换小品词后意为「接管」。

entries.definition: It is the plain verb for thinking about something; the phrase adds the idea of entering a calculation.
entries.definitionCN: 它只是「思考」的普通动词；本短语多出「纳入计算」之意。

entries.definition: It stresses setting aside room or time for a factor.
entries.definitionCN: 它强调为某因素留出余地或时间。

entries.definition: It is the business and statistical twin, common in modelling.
entries.definitionCN: 它是商业与统计语境的双胞胎，多见于建模。

entries.definition: It pictures putting things on a scale and judging between them.
entries.definitionCN: 它画出把东西放上天平、相互权衡的画面。

normalIntro.en: The normal associations use the real ledger image, the real verb pair and the contrast with taking for granted.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的账本意象、真实的动词配对以及与「想当然」的对比。

normal.en: An account is a ledger, so what is not entered does not count.
normal.cn: account 是账本，没有记入的就不算数。

normal.en: Into marks the movement from outside the book to inside it.
normal.cn: 介词标出从账外移入账内的动作。

normal.en: The phrase is stronger than consider: the factor must change the result.
normal.cn: 它比单纯「考虑」更强：因素必须改变结果。

normal.en: The negative form is how critics say a model missed something.
normal.cn: 否定式是批评者指出模型遗漏的方式。

normal.en: Take for granted is its opposite stance, not its synonym.
normal.cn: 「想当然」是它的反面，不是同义词。

abstract.en: Like a clerk spreading receipts on a desk and entering every one.
abstract.cn: 像账房先生把票据摊开，逐张记入。

abstract.en: Like packing a bag with the weight of the return trip already counted.
abstract.cn: 像打包行李时把回程的重量也算进去。

abstract.en: Like a scale that registers the last grain, not only the big weights.
abstract.cn: 像天平连最后一粒也记下，不只看大砝码。

examples.en: Any estimate must take into account the cost of maintenance.
examples.cn: 任何估算都必须把维护成本考虑在内。

examples.en: Teachers take into account the different starting points of students.
examples.cn: 教师会顾及学生不同的起点。

examples.en: The plan did not take into account the winter closure of the road.
examples.cn: 该计划没有把冬季封路考虑在内。

root: take 来自古诺斯语 taka「抓取」，中古英语时期取代本族动词；account 经古法语 acont 来自拉丁语 computare「计算」，由表示「一起」的前缀与 putare「思量」构成。该短语属近代用法，首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses split the phrase by what enters the account: a judgement, a figure, a person's needs, a risk, a balance of pros and cons, reserved time, an overlooked factor, a pre-decision stage and a model variable.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项按记入内容区分：判断、数字、他人需求、风险、利弊权衡、预留时间、被忽略的因素、决定前阶段、模型变量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clerk spreading receipts on a desk and entering each one in the ledger.
core.cn: 核心意象：账房先生把票据摊在桌上，逐张记入账本。

branches.en: THE JUDGEMENT: a factor enters before an opinion is fixed.
branches.cn: 判断：因素在意见定下之前进入。

branches.en: THE LEDGER: costs and reserved weeks become entries with numbers.
branches.cn: 账本：成本与预留周数变成带数字的条目。

branches.en: THE HUMAN SCALE: guests' needs and pros and cons are weighed together.
branches.cn: 人的尺度：客人需求与利弊一并权衡。

branches.en: THE MISSED RISK: hazards must be entered, and their absence is the criticism.
branches.cn: 遗漏的风险：危险必须记入，缺席即成批评点。

branches.en: THE MODEL: statistics lets a variable enter the equation.
branches.cn: 模型：统计学让变量进入方程。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Norse verb of grasping to a French-Latin noun of reckoning, so the affix set spans two language families.
intro.cn: 短语把北欧语「抓取」动词与法语—拉丁语「计算」名词组合起来，词缀因此横跨两个语族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin element is computare, to reckon, from com-, together, and putare, to think; the verb take has a Norse source.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语成分是 computare「计算」，由 com-「一起」与 putare「思量」构成；动词 take 来自北欧语。

items.example: The Norse verb replaced the native one in Middle English.
items.exampleCN: 这个北欧语动词在中古英语时期取代了本族词。

items.example: The verb is basic and highly productive.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词基础且极其能产。

items.example: The prefix makes the reckoning a joint one.
items.exampleCN: 前缀让计算成为合并的行为。

items.example: Its deeper origin has more than one explanation.
items.exampleCN: 其更深来源有不止一种解释。

items.example: The verb gives count, compute and account.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词给出「计数」「计算」「账目」诸词。

items.example: French carried the noun into English.
items.exampleCN: 法语把这个名词带入英语。

items.example: The noun keeps both money and explanation senses.
items.exampleCN: 名词兼有金钱与说明两义。

items.example: The frame fixes the factor after the noun.
items.exampleCN: 框架把因素固定在名词之后。

items.en: Cutten meant to slice or sever.

items.en: The ending -er named the doer of an action.
items.cn: 词尾 -er 表示动作的执行者。

items.en: The box cutter entered every warehouse.
